sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- subagent: For operator-requested delegation, use subagents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- context7_resolve-library-id: Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching...
- context7_query-docs: Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming...
- mcp: MCP gateway — install by URL, status, search, describe, auth, and single MCP tool calls
- ask_user_question: Ask the user up to 4 structured questions (2-4 options each) when requirements are ambiguous
- session_search: Semantic search over past pi sessions — find previous work, decisions, and context by topic.
- session_list: List/filter past pi sessions by project, date, or archive status.
- session_read: Read the full conversation from a specific past pi session by file path or ID.
- todo: Manage a task list to track multi-step progress
- web_search: Use for web research questions. Prefer {queries:[...]} with 2-4 varied angles over a single query for broader coverage. Omit provider unless explicitly overriding the configured default.
- source_check: Gather structured source evidence and passage-level citations for manual semantic review of a claim.
- fetch_content: Use to fetch URL content, direct images, GitHub repos, and videos.
- get_search_content: Use after web_search, source_check, or fetch_content to retrieve stored content via responseId. Use findText to locate passages without paging through the full content.
- web_enable: If tools for web search, source checking, content fetching, stored-result retrieval are not already available, call web_enable first whenever current, external, or linked information could help; the tools appear on the next model request.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Do not invoke subagents unless the operator requested delegation directly or through applicable instructions.
- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.
- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.
- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The "Type something." row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append "(Recommended)" to its label.
- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.
- Use session_search to find past coding sessions relevant to the current task (e.g. 'when did we refactor the auth module', 'previous work on Lambda timeouts').
- Pass the optional `project` parameter to limit search to a single project — use a substring of the project path or slug (e.g. 'pi-session-search').
- Use session_list for browsing by date/project. Use session_read to dive into a specific session.
- Use knowledge_search for conceptual queries (e.g. "how did we handle X", "what was decided about Y"). Use grep/read for exact text or known filenames.
- Use kb_read when a note is referenced by name or [[wikilink]] — don't run find/grep first.
- Use the standard `read` tool for non-indexed files or when you already have an absolute path.
- Use `todo` for complex work with 3+ steps, when the user gives you a list of tasks, or immediately after receiving new instructions to capture requirements. Skip it for single trivial tasks and purely conversational requests.
- When starting a task from the todo list, mark it in_progress BEFORE beginning work. Mark it completed IMMEDIATELY when done — never batch completions. Exactly one task in_progress at a time.
- Never mark a task completed if tests are failing, the implementation is partial, or you hit unresolved errors — keep it in_progress and create a new task for the blocker instead.
- Task status is a 4-state machine: pending → in_progress → completed, plus deleted as a tombstone. Pass activeForm (present-continuous label, e.g. 'researching existing tool') when marking in_progress.
- To change a task's status, call update with the task id and the target status, e.g. {"action":"update","id":3,"status":"completed"} or {"action":"update","id":3,"status":"in_progress","activeForm":"writing tests"}. status is the field that changes the task; an update without a mutable field (status or another) is rejected.
- Use blockedBy to express dependencies (A is blocked by B). On create, pass blockedBy as the initial set. On update, use addBlockedBy / removeBlockedBy (additive merge — do not resend the full array). Cycles are rejected.
- list hides tombstoned (deleted) tasks by default; pass includeDeleted:true to see them. Pass status to filter by a single status.
- Subject must be short and imperative (e.g. 'Research existing tool'); description is for long-form detail. activeForm is a present-continuous label shown while in_progress.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

<project_context>
Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/home/nobody/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md">
# AGENTS.md

## Global rules

1. **IMPORTANT** **NEVER COMMIT AND PUSH FILES THAT ARE MARKED AS IGNORED IN GIT, NO EXCEPTIONS!**
2. Store temp/debug files in `/tmp/`, **NEVER COMMIT TEMP/DEBUG FILES**
3. ONLY modify files within the current repository root (resolved via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).
   If not in a git repository: ASK user to confirm before modifying any files; if confirmed, treat CWD as root.
   Exception: temp/debug files MAY be written to `/tmp/`.
   All other paths outside the repo root require explicit user confirmation.
4. NEVER read, print, or modify any file that may contain secrets or credentials — including
   `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*_key`, `*-key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.cert`, `*credentials*`,
   `*secret*`, `*_token`, `*-token` files, or any file containing values that appear to be
   API keys, passwords, or private keys.
   Exception: sanitized example files where every secret-shaped value is replaced with a
   descriptive placeholder (e.g. `your-token-here`, `<PLACEHOLDER>`, `changeme`).
5. BEFORE new services, schema/model changes, new modules, cross-cutting pattern changes,
   deletes, force-pushes, or any other irreversible action → present viable options with
   trade-offs and ask user to choose. If only one viable option exists, state it and explain why.
   Minor reversible changes (local variable names, comment wording, formatting) → proceed and
   state the assumption.
6. Please put agent generated spec files in (creater path if it doesn't exist): `<repository root>/docs/agent/specs/`.
7. Please put agfent generated plan files in (creater path if it doesn't exist): `<repository root>/docs/agent/plans/`.

## Authentication

For authentication flows (GitHub, AWS, Azure), load the `harness` skill
and follow the Authentication Flows section for your detected harness. Run auth flows
only when the current task requires access to the listed provider.

## MCP server routing

For available MCP servers and their routing, load the `harness` skill
and check the MCP Server Routing table for your detected harness. Only use servers
marked as available for your environment.

## Chains and Skills

Use the following prompt templates for common workflows. They invoke skills and chain steps automatically — do NOT bypass them by loading skills directly unless the chain doesn't cover your case.

| Workflow | Command | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fix bugs | `/chain-fix` | Debug → TDD → Verify → Tech-debt → Code-review → QA → Finalise |
| Implement feature | `/chain-implement` | Plan → Sub-agents → Verify → Tech-debt → Code-review → QA → Finalise |
| QA pass | `/chain-qa` | Verify → Tech-debt → Code-review → QA → Finalise |
| Design spec | `/chain-spec` | Harness → Context → Create-spec |
| Code review | `/prompt-code-review` | Single-shot code review with two reviewers |
| Release review | `/prompt-release-review` | Full review + code smell analysis |
| Tech debt | `/prompt-tech-debt` | Coverage, CRAP, README, docstrings |
| Finalise branch | `/prompt-finalising` | Present the skill's integration options for the detected mode and branch |

**When using a chain: each step has a specific job. Do ONLY that job.** The chain handles progression. Do not skip ahead, do not dispatch work that belongs to a later step.

## Critical Rules for Correct Behaviour

### 1. Subagent dispatch — you MUST verify the actual code, not your intent

When dispatching multiple sub-agents in parallel (e.g. two code reviewers), you MUST:

1. **WRITE** the full subagent() call into a code block in your response first
2. **COUNT** the number of `{ agent:` lines in the code block you just wrote
3. **Only dispatch** if the count is exactly 2 and the model values are different
4. If you have only 1, fix the call before proceeding — do not dispatch

**Do NOT trust your mental count.** The mental check is unreliable. Read what you actually wrote. This rule exists because agents consistently say "2 entries ✅" then dispatch 1.

### 2. User decisions — use the tool, not prose

If you uncover a question the user needs to answer (architectural choice, which approach, scope approval, etc.):

- **Use `ask_user_question`** with clear options
- Do NOT write the question in prose and hope something stops to wait for an answer
- Prose questions are invisible to the chain — it will silently skip to the next step

### 3. Verification before claims

Do NOT claim "done", "fixed", "passing", or any success state without running fresh verification commands. See the `verify` skill for the full process. In short:

- Run the command
- Read the output
- Check the exit code
- THEN make the claim

Trusting a previous run, an agent report, or your confidence is not verification.

### 4. Changes must be scoped to the chain step

Each chain step has a defined scope (see the prompt template body):

- `debugging`: investigate only — do NOT fix
- `tdd`: test-first implementation only — do NOT skip RED phase
- `verify`: run commands and report — do NOT fix issues found
- `tech-debt`: coverage, CRAP, README, docstrings — do NOT run full lint/type stack (qa-gate handles that)
- `code-review`: dispatch reviewers, fix issues, repeat — do NOT push or commit
- `qa-gate`: run all gates — do NOT fix code
- `finalising`: present options, execute choice, show summary — do NOT dispatch sub-agents

## Required Standards

*Mandatory style rules applied when writing code. Where project-local conventions conflict
with these standards, project-local conventions take precedence — unless they violate
security rules (Global rule 3).*

### Code style

- Security first — no exceptions.
- Verify before assuming — use `context7` first; fall back to web search (no MCP required)
  if `context7` is unavailable or lacks the needed docs.
- DRY, KISS, single responsibility, no deep nesting.
- Error handling and edge cases required on all code paths.
- Follow existing patterns in the project.
- Prefer ASCII characters in all comments and code. Use Unicode only when the logic requires it.
- Do not embed more than 5 lines of another language inline; extract to a dedicated file instead.

### Bash

Style guide: [Google Bash Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/shellguide.html).
Local rules below take precedence on any conflicts.

- `snake_case` variables/functions; `ALL_CAPS` globals.
- Max line length: 120 characters.
- `local` for all variables declared inside functions; top-level script variables use direct assignment.
- Quote scalar variable expansions: `"${VAR}"`.
  Where unquoted expansion is intentional (arrays, globs, arithmetic), add an inline comment:
  `# shellcheck disable=<shellcheck code>`.
- Two-space indent; `[[` not `[`; `set -euo pipefail` at top of every script.
- RUN `shellcheck <script>` on all created or modified shell scripts.
  If ShellCheck is unavailable: STOP and report before finalising any shell changes.
- `set -x` for debugging only — remove before finalising.

### Python

**Tooling** (applies when no existing Python workflow is detected; otherwise follow the
existing toolchain). Existing workflow indicators: `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`,
`noxfile.py`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, or a `Makefile` with a `test` target.
Default toolchain: `uv` (not pip), `mypy` + `ruff` (linting), `pre-commit`, `pytest`.
Prefer `uv run` for all Python commands — it does not require venv activation.
If `uv` is unavailable and `.venv` exists: use `.venv/bin/python -m <command>` per invocation
(do not `source .venv/bin/activate` — env changes may not persist across processes).
If neither `uv` nor `.venv` exists: STOP and report before running any Python commands.
New projects: prefer `click` for CLI and `loguru` for logging — confirm with user before adding
any new dependency (Global rule 4).

**Naming:**

- ALL exception class names MUST use `CapWords` and MUST end with `Error` (e.g. `NetworkError`).
  Derive from `Exception`, not `BaseException`.
- Non-public: `_name`; name-mangled: `__attr` (double prefix, inside a body).
- Never `l`, `O`, `I` as single-character names.

**Code rules:**

- `None` comparisons: `is`/`is not`, never `==`.
- Catch specific exceptions; no bare `except:`.
- `with` for resource management.
- `raise X from Y` for exception chaining.
- Consistent `return` — all values or all `None`, never mixed.
- `''.join()` over `+=` in loops.
- `__all__` in public `__init__.py` files and dedicated re-export modules (not required in
  tests, scripts, or internal helper modules).
- PEP 484 type hints on all functions; space after `:` and around `->`.
- Docstrings required on all functions and classes with no leading `_`, and on all modules.
  Not required on dunder methods or test functions.
- f-strings for formatting.
- Classes for data+behaviour groupings; functions otherwise. (Advisory: use judgment.)
- Max 50 non-blank physical lines per function/method (excluding decorators and docstrings).

**QC — run in this order for Python changes:**

1. `uv run ruff check --fix . && uv run ruff format .`
   Fix issues introduced by the current change; pre-existing issues in unmodified files
   may be noted but are not required fixes unless they block CI.
2. `uv run mypy .` — fix all type errors.
3. Coverage:
   - Single package (one `__init__.py`): `uv run pytest --cov=<pkg> --cov-fail-under=80 -v`
     (replace `<pkg>` with the affected top-level package directory)
   - Multiple packages changed: run once per affected package.
   - Script-only repos (no `__init__.py`): `uv run pytest -v` (omit `--cov` flags).
   - Fix all test failures.
4. If `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists: `pre-commit run --all-files` — final gate.
   If `pre-commit` is unavailable: STOP and report before finalising.

**Testing guideline:** Test through the public API. Do not call private methods (`_name`) in tests.

### Markdown

Detect tool (check config AND binary availability):

1. If (`.markdownlint-cli2.*` or `.markdownlintrc` exists) AND `markdownlint-cli2` is installed
   → `markdownlint-cli2 --fix <file>`
2. Else if `markdownlint` is installed → `markdownlint --fix <file>`
3. Else: STOP and report before finalising any markdown changes.

Line length up to 120 characters permitted; no limit in tables.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: subagent
toolsAdded.description:
Delegate one child with {agent,task?}; otherwise set exactly one workflow source, with optional args.
Workflow script: write it as one ```js workflow block in this reply, then call subagent({workflow:true,...}). workflow:'./path.js' (any value with '/') loads a file from request cwd; other strings name a resource.
agent/task exclude workflow; task excludes action. agent may target management actions. action is management/control; validate accepts workflow:true or a path without launching.
Scripts: JavaScript statement bodies with explicit return, top-level await, plain helpers/Promise chains; nested async function/arrow/method helpers are rejected. Await runs.run('key',{agent,task}) before .output; await runs.all([{key,agent,task},...]) for an ordered array, not a key map. Observe every stored run promise with direct await, Promise.race or Promise.all. Await/return runs.steer(key,message,options?) for a prior key, never raw run ids; queued/delivered/missed/failed receipts are not compliance proof.
Before advanced orchestration (runs.lanes, rolling fanout, mission state, handoffs), read {action:"guide",topic:"workflows"} or the pi-subagents skill. Raw-script sandboxes add deeply frozen args; all sandboxes provide runs, emit, console, JavaScript and enabled mission state, with no filesystem/shell/Pi tools/host globals. External CLI agents support native options only when their runner declares them; read guide tool-reference before passing model, structured output, acceptance/agentContract, tool budget, fast, fork context or skills/tools.
Model override: first call {action:"models"}; copy exact provider/id, not agent names. Thinking uses model suffix, not watchdog-only thinking.
Named resources: {workflow:'review',args:{task:'...'}} or {workflow:'run-ci',args:{command:'npm test'}}. Raw scripts also accept bounded plain-data args; raw-script args persist as evidence, so never include secrets. worktree:true requires clean source; baseRef defaults to HEAD at allocation or a supported named ref, never full 40/64-character commit IDs or revision expressions.

SAFETY-CRITICAL SUBAGENT GUIDANCE:
• Direct parent execution is the default. Invoke subagents only when delegation is authorized by the operator's current request or applicable user/project instructions; task size, complexity, risk, tool-call count, or recipe fit do not independently authorize delegation.
• First call {action:"list",capabilities:true}: executable, non-disabled agents only; external-cli requires runner.available === true. Passive PATH/PATHEXT/X_OK is not authentication/version/launch proof; preflight is authoritative.
• Workflow, child launch, prompt runtime, extension load or child tooling failure is a lane infrastructure blocker. Stop; report exact failure, run/status and repo/cwd/worktree/branch/ref; verify clean worktree or capture partial diff before same-protocol retry or asking the owner. Never silently switch to interactive_shell, pi -ne, Codex/Claude/Cursor CLI or foreground/external mode: governed-workflow fallback requires explicit owner approval, not Pi core's generic pi -ne hint. Explicit foreground/CLI requests and work outside that protocol remain valid.
• Omit action for execution. For an authorized delegated multi-step/parallel workflow: exactly one top-level subagent workflow call with async:true; children launch only inside it.
• Async follows asyncByDefault (normally true); async:false only to block the parent, not for final reviews/gates. Consume results at dependency barriers. Native async completion wakes this session: return control, no sleep/poll or bg_wait merely for a wake. bg_wait is for provider/detached work without native notification needing a same-turn result.
• Ordinary child subagents are not orchestrators; only configured fanout within depth/session limits. For an authorized delegated workflow, keep one writer per cwd/worktree and isolate concurrent writers. Use fresh-context read-only reviewers when independent review was requested, then parent synthesis/fixes. Oracle/advisor unknowns use supervisor dialogue; one-shot only when requested.
• Bind durable output on runs.run/runs.all, not task filename prose; return actual outputReference/outputPathMapping/artifactPaths, evidence and residual risks.
• children.list is workflow-only, not an exhaustive list of direct native children: resume only resumable rows. When an intended child's exact run id is known, inspect it with {action:"status",id}; if status identifies the candidate, attempt {action:"resume",id,message}. Resume authoritatively checks eligibility, may reject it, and otherwise detaches a follow-up/challenge with the stored agent/model/tool contract. Use a labeled same-role fallback only when no known candidate exists or resume rejects eligibility. Scripts await runs.run(newKey,{resume:runId,task}); continue from latest returned runId. Each distinct resume pass needs a new stable key; same-key reuse requires identical launch parameters.
• Named resources own authority; raw scripts (workflow:true or a path) cannot use runs.host. Granted commands/relative outputs use workflow cwd, never per-step cwd.
• Inspect asyncId/asyncDir (status.json, events.jsonl, logs) with status/debug.run; control with interrupt/stop/resume/steer. For local Pi children explicitly granted subagent_command, command.status/yield/cancel targets one exact toolCallId without interrupting the child. Read {action:"guide",topic:"tool-reference"} for controls/evidence gates.

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background, provider, or detached work that has no native completion notification, then return.

Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively when they complete or need attention. In an interactive chat, return control instead of calling this merely to wait. Use this tool for provider jobs, remembered detached foreground runs, or other background work without a native notification path. Headless runs auto-drain current-session subagent work at agent_end; use this tool only when the current turn must receive non-notifying background work results.

• { } — return when the first initially active async run or registered provider item finishes, or when a subagent needs attention.
• { all: true } — wait for every async run, provider item, and remembered detached foreground descendant that was active when the call began.
• { id: "..." } — wait for one async or remembered detached foreground subagent run (id or prefix). Named async runs that already finished return their terminal result references.
• { id: "...", nonBlocking: true } — resolve the prefix once, persist an exact-run wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this for detached work without native completion delivery; the originating interactive session wakes on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout.
• { stopOnAttention: false } — for blocking waits only, keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.
• { timeoutMs: 600000 } — stop waiting after N ms; active work keeps running. Omitted values use waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 minutes. Window expiry returns a non-error window_elapsed result with active work identities.

Non-blocking subscriptions are visible in subagent status and differ from disabling waitTool: waitTool.enabled=false returns immediately without registering any future wake. Provider jobs are session-scoped and identified exactly, so replacing one job with another cannot hide a completion. Provider extensions must be explicitly loaded in this process. In a child agent, keep `bg_wait` in the child tool allowlist and load each provider through the agent's extensions or subagentOnlyExtensions; this tool never loads providers or grants tools itself.

id.description: Async run or remembered detached foreground run id/prefix to wait for one specific run. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use bg_wait for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, or when same-turn blocking results are truly needed. Omit to wait across every active async run started in this session only when a same-turn wait is truly needed.

nonBlocking.description: When true, resolve id to one exact run, persist a wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this only for provider, detached, or other background work without a native completion notification; ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively and do not need a subscription. The originating session is woken on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout. Requires id and cannot be combined with all.

all.description: Wait for ALL active runs to finish. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use all only when a same-turn result from tracked background work is truly needed. Default false: return when the first tracked run or provider item finishes or needs attention. Ignored when id targets a single run.

timeoutMs.description: Give up waiting after this many milliseconds (the runs keep going regardless). Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use a wait timeout only when same-turn results are truly needed for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification. Defaults to config waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 1800000 (30 minutes). Window expiry is a non-error active-work result.

stopOnAttention.description: For a blocking wait that is truly needed, stop when a run needs attention by default. Set false to keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.

toolsAdded.name: context7_resolve-library-id
toolsAdded.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation. This is used to rank library results by relevance to what the user is trying to accomplish. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

libraryName.description: Library name to search for and retrieve a Context7-compatible library ID. Use the official library name with proper punctuation — e.g., 'Next.js' instead of 'nextjs', 'Customer.io' instead of 'customerio', 'Three.js' instead of 'threejs'.

toolsAdded.name: context7_query-docs
toolsAdded.description:
Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework.

You must call 'Resolve Context7 Library ID' tool first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question.

libraryId.description: Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., '/mongodb/docs', '/vercel/next.js', '/supabase/supabase', '/vercel/next.js/v14.3.0-canary.87') retrieved from 'resolve-library-id' or directly from user query in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version'.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation, scoped to a single concept. Be specific and include relevant details, but keep each query to one topic — if the user's question spans multiple distinct concepts, make a separate call per concept instead of combining them, unless the question is about how the concepts interact. Good: 'How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js' or 'React useEffect cleanup function examples'. Bad (too vague): 'auth' or 'hooks'. Bad (too broad): 'routing and auth and caching in Next.js'. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

toolsAdded.name: mcp
toolsAdded.description:
MCP gateway — URL installation, server status, tool search/describe, auth, and single MCP tool calls. When a user supplies an MCP endpoint URL, install it with the install action. Non-MCP Pi tools should be called directly, not through mcp.

Servers: context7, github

Usage:
  mcp({ action: "install", url: "https://example.com/mcp" }) → Install, connect, and authenticate an MCP URL
  mcp({ })                              → Show server status and tool counts
  mcp({ server: "name" })               → List tools from server
  mcp({ search: "query" })              → Search MCP tools by name/description
  mcp({ describe: "tool_name" })        → Show tool details and parameters
  mcp({ instructions: "name" })         → Show full server usage instructions
  mcp({ connect: "server-name" })       → Connect to a server and refresh metadata
  mcp({ tool: "name", args: { key: "value" } })         → Call a tool (object args; JSON string also accepted)
  mcp({ action: "ui-messages" })        → Retrieve accumulated messages from completed UI sessions
  mcp({ action: "auth-start", server: "name" })      → Open OAuth and watch for completion
  mcp({ action: "auth-complete", server: "name", args: { redirectUrl: "..." } }) → Complete manual OAuth

Mode: action > tool (call) > connect > describe > instructions > search > server (list) > nothing (status)

args.description: Tool arguments as a JSON object, or as a JSON string encoding one

connect.description: Server name to connect (lazy connect + metadata refresh)

instructions.description: Server name to show that server's usage instructions

searchMode.description: Search backend (default: lexical; semantic is available when a System One key is configured)

regex.description: Treat search as regex (default: substring match)

includeSchemas.description: Include parameter schemas in search results (default: true)

server.description: Server name: filters searches, disambiguates calls and describe operations, and optionally names an install

toolsAdded.name: ask_user_question
toolsAdded.description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions during execution. Use when you need to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions
3. Get decisions on implementation choices as you work
4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take

Usage notes:
- Users can type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.
- Use multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. The "Type something." row is available on every question, including when options carry a `preview`; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column.
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: MAX 16 CHARACTERS — hard limit, requests over the limit are rejected. Very short chip/tag shown next to the question. Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

label.description: MAX 60 CHARACTERS — hard limit, requests over the limit are rejected. The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). The 'Type something.' row is appended automatically — do NOT author it.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

Status: pending → in_progress → completed, plus deleted tombstone. Use this to plan and track multi-step work like research, design, and implementation.

toolsAdded.name: web_search
toolsAdded.description: Search the web with OpenAI, Brave, Parallel, Parallel MCP, TinyFish, Search1API, Searchinfinity, Querit, Tavily, You.com, Firecrawl, Jina, SearXNG, degoog, DuckDuckGo, Perplexity, Gemini, Kimi, Exa, SERPdive, Kagi, Ollama, Anysearch, xAI, Mistral, Bright Data, SerpBase, SerpApi, Serper, Serply, Valyu, Bocha, XCrawl, Baizhi, Z.ai, Keenable. Provider arrays run simultaneously; all searches eligible allowed providers (OpenAI, Brave, Parallel, TinyFish, Search1API, Searchinfinity, Querit, Tavily, Firecrawl, Jina, SearXNG, Perplexity, Gemini, Exa, SERPdive, Kagi, Ollama, Bocha); explicit-only allowed providers (Parallel MCP, You.com, degoog, DuckDuckGo, Kimi, Anysearch, xAI, Mistral, Bright Data, SerpBase, SerpApi, Serper, Serply, Valyu, XCrawl, Baizhi, Z.ai, Keenable) remain excluded. The default workflow is none: it returns bounded source-linked search results or provider answers without a curator or generated summary, identifies the providers used, and stores full results for retrieval by responseId. For comprehensive research, prefer queries (plural) with 2-4 varied angles over a single query. When includeContent is true, full page content is fetched in the background. Set workflow to "summary-review" to open the curator with an auto-generated summary draft or "auto-summary" to generate a summary without the browser curator. The configured provider is used when provider is omitted or set to auto; omit provider unless explicitly overriding it.

query.description: Single search query. For research tasks, prefer 'queries' with multiple varied angles instead.

queries.description: Multiple queries searched concurrently (up to three at a time), each returning source-linked search results or a provider answer. Prefer this for research — vary phrasing, scope, and angle across 2-4 queries to maximize coverage. Good: ['React vs Vue performance benchmarks 2026', 'React vs Vue developer experience comparison', 'React ecosystem size vs Vue ecosystem']. Bad: ['React vs Vue', 'React vs Vue comparison', 'React vs Vue review'] (too similar, redundant results).

domainFilter.description: Limit to domains (prefix with - to exclude)

category.description: Exa only: result category, e.g. news, research paper

provider.description: Search provider or non-empty list of allowed providers to search simultaneously; all searches eligible allowed providers (OpenAI, Brave, Parallel, TinyFish, Search1API, Searchinfinity, Querit, Tavily, Firecrawl, Jina, SearXNG, Perplexity, Gemini, Exa, SERPdive, Kagi, Ollama, Bocha); explicit-only allowed providers (Parallel MCP, You.com, degoog, DuckDuckGo, Kimi, Anysearch, xAI, Mistral, Bright Data, SerpBase, SerpApi, Serper, Serply, Valyu, XCrawl, Baizhi, Z.ai, Keenable) remain excluded; omit this field to use the configured provider, or use auto when none is configured

workflow.description: Search workflow mode: none = no curator (default), summary-review = open curator with auto summary draft, auto-summary = generate summary without opening curator

proxy.description: http(s) or socks proxy URL (e.g. http://host:port or socks5h://host:port) used for every outbound request in this call (search APIs and content fetches). Node fetch ignores HTTP(S)_PROXY env vars, so set this (or `proxy` in web-search.json) when direct access is blocked; empty string forces direct access.

fetchContent.description: Fetch up to 5 result pages for exact passage extraction.

domainFilter.description: Limit to domains; prefix with - to exclude.

provider.description: Search provider or non-empty list of allowed providers to search simultaneously; all searches eligible allowed providers (OpenAI, Brave, Parallel, TinyFish, Search1API, Searchinfinity, Querit, Tavily, Firecrawl, Jina, SearXNG, Perplexity, Gemini, Exa, SERPdive, Kagi, Ollama, Bocha); explicit-only allowed providers (Parallel MCP, You.com, degoog, DuckDuckGo, Kimi, Anysearch, xAI, Mistral, Bright Data, SerpBase, SerpApi, Serper, Serply, Valyu, XCrawl, Baizhi, Z.ai, Keenable) remain excluded

proxy.description: http(s) or socks proxy URL (e.g. http://host:port or socks5h://host:port) used for every outbound request in this call (search APIs and result-page fetches). Empty string forces direct access.

toolsAdded.name: fetch_content
toolsAdded.description: Fetch URL(s). Available modes: readable (default): extract readable content as markdown; raw: return the exact textual body using direct HTTP only; answer: answer a prompt using only fetched content. Direct image URLs return resized image content when supported by the selected mode. Supports YouTube transcripts, GitHub repositories, PDFs, and local videos when supported by the selected mode. Full original content is stored for retrieval with get_search_content.

# seakarr

Automated Soulseek music downloader with library quality upgrading.

## Features

- **Library quality scanner** — walks your music library directories, reads audio tags (FLAC, MP3, AAC,
  OGG, Opus, WAV, WMA, and more via [lofty](https://crates.io/crates/lofty)), and identifies albums
  whose tracks are in a format outside `filters.allowed_extensions` or fall below the
  configurable bitrate threshold.
- **Upgrade mode** — for each album needing an upgrade, searches the Soulseek network, ranks
  candidates by advertised speed (adjusted by measured-throughput reputation), free-slot bonus, bitrate bonus,
  album-name match and peer reliability, and downloads the best match. The result is written into your
  library when the artist already has a folder under a configured `library.paths` entry, and stays in
  `storage.staging_dir` when it does not; an album selected by `library_upgrade.enabled` is replaced in
  place. An upgrade whose every destination already holds a strictly better file
  keeps those files and still completes the album, so the staging copy is removed without a new file being
  written. A candidate whose files omit the bitrate attribute scores zero on the bitrate bonus once
  `filters.min_bit_rate` is set, so a peer that reports one is preferred; it is still admitted, because its
  real quality is verified after download.
- **Discover mode** — derives the artist list from your library (tags first,
  folder names as the fallback), keeps only the artists that own a folder of
  their own, asks MusicBrainz which conceptual albums each of those is missing,
  and downloads only those. An artist the library only knows as a guest inside
  another artist's folder is skipped, and the run summary reports how many were
  skipped that way; name one explicitly with `--artist` to process it anyway.
  Naming an artist explicitly does not require the library to hold an album for
  it: when a folder named after the artist exists, the artist is processed and
  its albums are placed into that folder, and when there is neither an album nor
  a folder the run warns and keeps the downloads in staging.
  Albums already present are never
  searched or re-downloaded, and each run stops after
  `discover.max_cycle_downloads` download attempts so a large library fills in
  over successive runs. Release types come from `discography.allowed_types`.
- **Manual & batch modes** — search for a specific artist/album on demand, or process a newline-separated
  text file of `artist - album` lines to download a curated wantlist.
  A run places each completed album into the artist's existing library folder when one exists
  anywhere under a configured `library.paths` entry; when the artist has no folder there, or the
  album's destination folder already exists, a manual run keeps the download in
  `storage.staging_dir` (batch and upgrade runs merge into the existing folder instead, keeping
  any file that already parses as audio). An
  album-only request names no artist, so it always stays in staging and says nothing: only manual
  mode can express one, because upgrade mode rejects `--album` on its own and a batch line is trimmed
  before it is parsed, so a line written as `" - Album"` is read as an artist-only line. An artist-naming run with a configured library path explains a
  staging-only download once it has one.
- **Authoritative artist discography** — artist-only manual runs resolve conceptual albums from MusicBrainz
  release groups (cached locally for 30 days) and then run one sequential `Artist Album` Soulseek search per
  eligible album, oldest first. The same authoritative resolution powers `discover` mode for every artist
  it sweeps — those that own a folder named after them. Release categories and optional MusicBrainz artist IDs are configurable; the
  previous folder heuristic remains the explicit opt-out and the visible fallback.
- **Quality filtering** — filter Soulseek results by file extension, minimum
  bitrate, excluded keywords, and upload availability. With
  `download.max_queue_length: 0` a peer must offer a free upload slot; a
  positive limit also admits zero-slot peers until their reported queue
  position can be validated. Path-traversal names are rejected.
- **Peer reputation** — remembers each peer's effective throughput (bytes ÷ transfer time: retry delays plus
  the final transfer, excluding queue wait) and success rate (in SQLite), and ranks search results by a blend
  of advertised and measured throughput plus a reliability factor, so fast, reliable peers are preferred and
  slow or error-prone peers are demoted — regardless of what you search for. Controlled by

## Design — nested staging album layout (`src/staging.rs`)

### 1. Architecture and components

A new module `src/staging.rs` owns the staging layout rule; `organizer.rs` keeps library-write concerns. Four public items:

```rust
/// <staging_dir>/<sanitised artist>            (sanitize_component yields "_" for a blank artist)
pub fn artist_dir(staging_dir: &Path, artist: &str) -> PathBuf;
/// <staging_dir>/<sanitised artist>/<sanitised album>
pub fn album_dir(staging_dir: &Path, artist: &str, album: &str) -> PathBuf;

/// One album found under the staging root, with its identity resolved from the
/// processed-album table (None when no row matches: an untracked leftover).
pub struct StagedAlbum {
    pub album_dir: PathBuf,
    pub artist_dir_path: PathBuf,
    pub dir_album: String,
    pub identity: Option<StagedIdentity>, // { artist, album, status } - raw names from the DB
}
pub fn scan(staging_dir: &Path, db: &Database) -> Result<Vec<StagedAlbum>>;

/// Rename legacy `<artist>--<album>` folders into the nested form and drop
/// artist folders that hold nothing.
pub fn normalise_layout(staging_dir: &Path) -> Result<MigrationReport>;
```

`runner.rs:512` becomes `staging::album_dir(staging_dir, artist, album)`; every other staging path in `runner.rs` (`finish_library_write`, `discard_refused_staging`) derives from that one value, so the layout rule exists in one place. `organizer::parse_album_slug` **stays**, but only as the legacy parser `normalise_layout` uses — it is no longer used by recovery. `disc_subdir` takes the album string it can already see and stops walking when the directory name equals `sanitize_component(album)` instead of sniffing `"--"`.

*Does section 1 look right?*

### 2. Data flow

1. `process_albums` creates the staging root, then calls `staging::normalise_layout` (unconditional — the layout rule applies to every mode), then `organizer::recover_interrupted_upgrades` (unchanged gate: `library_upgrade.enabled` and a configured library path).
2. `process_album_internal` builds `album_staging = staging::album_dir(...)`; `download_album` creates it lazily and nests disc folders inside it exactly as today — no change to `download.rs`, because it receives the finished path.
3. On a library write, `finish_library_write` removes the album dir and then prunes its parent with `fs::remove_dir`; `discard_refused_staging` does the same once `remove_empty_staging_dirs` has emptied it. `remove_dir` refuses a non-empty directory, so a sibling album of the same artist staged concurrently is never touched.
4. Recovery iterates `staging::scan(...)` output and keeps its current two arms — `success` → `resume_library_upgrade(config, album_dir, library_root, raw artist, raw album)`, anything else → `remove_dir_all`. `resume_library_upgrade` and its library-write half are unchanged.

*Does section 2 look right?*

### 3. Legacy migration

`normalise_layout` walks the top level of the staging root:

- A directory whose name contains `--` is a legacy slug: split on the **first** `--` (today's rule), sanitise both halves, `create_dir_all` the artist dir, then `fs::rename` the legacy dir onto `<artist>/<album>`.
- If `<artist>/<album>` already exists, merge without overwriting: rename each child that is not already present at the destination and count it; when a name collides, the destination file stays and the legacy copy is left where it is. A legacy dir that still holds skipped entries is left in place and reported; one that is emptied is removed.
- A top-level name with no `--` is already an artist dir: it is left alone, and removed only if it holds nothing at all.
- A name that is not valid UTF-8 is left untouched with a warning: renaming it through `to_string_lossy` would invent characters and could orphan a recoverable album.

Per-entry failures are logged and counted, never fatal — the caller already treats a failed staging pass as a warning (`runner.rs:1469`), and a wasted rename must not stop a download run.

*Does section 3 look right?*

### 4. Recovery identity, and the edges

`scan` reads `db.get_processed_albums()` **once** per run and matches each `<artist>/<album>` directory against rows by comparing `sanitize_component(row.artist)` / `sanitize_component(row.album)` case-insensitively with the two directory names. A match yields the row's **raw** names and status, so `resume_library_upgrade` copies to the same library path (sanitising is idempotent) and the status write keeps the raw key. When several rows match, the highest `id` wins and the ambiguity is warned about, so a shared sanitised name still recovers the most recent successful one. No row → `identity: None` → the leftover is cleaned exactly as today.

Edge cases, each with a stated outcome: a blank artist (album-only run) stages under the `_` placeholder — uniform two-level layout, and no DB row means recovery cleans it exactly as it cleans `--Album` today; a legacy dir with no separator that holds no subdirectory is left alone and reported rather than deleted, because the nested layout makes "files directly in a top-level dir" ambiguous with real content; an album literally named `Disc 1` is unaffected because `disc_subdir` still returns the *innermost* match and the album root comparison only stops the upward walk. Staging inside a library path stays a documented misconfiguration, not a new validation — out of scope here.

*Does section 4 look right?*

### 5. Testing and documentation

Unit tests in `staging.rs`: both components sanitised; blank artist → `_`; migration of `A--B` to `A/B`; merge keeps the existing destination file and moves the rest; a still-populated legacy dir is reported not deleted; empty artist dirs pruned; a non-UTF-8 name skipped (`#[cfg(unix)]`); `scan` resolving raw names case-insensitively, returning `None` for an unknown dir, and choosing the highest `id` when two rows match. Updated in place: `organizer.rs` recovery tests move to nested paths (the `Unknown--Album` fixture), `tests/pipeline_test.rs` expects `Test Artist/Test Album` and asserts no empty artist dir survives, and `runner.rs` `discard_refused_staging` / `finish_library_write` / album-only staging tests assert the new shape. `download.rs` tests are untouched — it never sees the layout. TDD: the failing test for each unit lands before its production code.

Documentation: a new dated spec at `docs/agent/specs/<date>-nested-staging-layout-design.md` plus its plan in `docs/agent/plans/`. The historical specs that record `<artist>--<album>` (`2026-09-15-discover-library-placement-design.md`, `2026-09-23-remove-organize-design.md`) are left as written history; the README describes `staging_dir` without naming the layout, so it needs no change — that stays true only if the final code has no user-visible layout string in the README tables, which the spec will state as a check for the plan.

| Library-write path | Artist component | Album / file components |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy_to_library` (upgrade) — `organizer.rs:328` → `library_relative_path:129-134` | `sanitize_component(artist)` | `sanitize_component(album/track/title/ext)` |
| `place_into_library` (upgrade/auto/discover/manual placement) → `album_dir_for:155` | on-disk folder name, **used verbatim** | `sanitize_component(album)` |
| `delete_lesser_quality_files:552` | sanitised | sanitised |
| `resume_library_upgrade:697-698` (+ per-entry leaf `:723/728`) | sanitised | sanitised |
| `disc_subdir:531` (disc label becomes a real folder) | n/a | sanitised |
| `search.rs:1211-1256`, `discover.rs:319` (library lookups, both sides) | sanitised | sanitised |
| staged file names (`download.rs`) | n/a | peer basename only, safe-basename checked; never a library folder |

So the only place an artist *folder name* reaches the filesystem unsanitised is `place_into_library`, and that is deliberate: that string is the name of an artist folder that **already exists** on disk (found by the library walk or `ArtistFolderIndex`), and the whole point of placement is to write into that existing folder rather than create a differently-named one. Re-sanitising it there would not add safety — `album_dir_for` already rejects anything that is not a single ordinary path component — it would just split one artist into two folders. The album below it is sanitised either way. Every folder seakarr *creates* comes from a sanitised name.

**What this adds to the spec — a new section 6, "Sanitisation consistency":**

- Requirement: one rule, one function — every production path that turns an artist or album string into a path component calls `sanitize_component` at the moment the name is created; no second sanitiser, no per-mode variant. Staging joins that set.
- The audit table above, recorded in the spec as the state the change must preserve.
- The single documented exception, with its guard (`place_into_library` + `album_dir_for`), so a later reader cannot mistake it for an oversight.

# Nested staging album layout

## Problem

A staged album is one directory named `<artist>--<album>` directly under
`storage.staging_dir`, so a download that stays in staging reads as
`downloads/staging/Artist Name--Album Name/01 - Track.flac`. The operator wants the
two components to be real directories instead:
`downloads/staging/Artist Name/Album Name/01 - Track.flac`.

The flattened name is not only cosmetic. It is a lossy encoding of two values into one
path component, and the code that consumes it has to decode it again:

| Site | Behaviour today |
| --- | --- |
| `src/runner.rs:508-516` | Builds `format!("{}--{}", artist.replace(['/','\\'], "-"), album.unwrap_or("unknown").replace(['/','\\'], "-"))` and joins it to the staging root. |
| `src/organizer.rs:516-533` `disc_subdir` | Walks a staged file's parent directories and stops when a directory name `.contains("--")`, because that names the album staging root. An album whose own name contains `--` cannot be told from a boundary by this test. |
| `src/organizer.rs:758-763` `parse_album_slug` | Splits on the first `--` to recover `(artist, album)`; a name without a separator becomes album `"Unknown"`. |
| `src/organizer.rs:774-810` `recover_interrupted_upgrades` | Reads the top level of the staging root, treats every directory as an album slug, re-verifies a `success` album by copying it back, and deletes every other leftover. |
| `src/runner.rs:355-389` `discard_refused_staging` | Removes a refused album's staged files, then prunes directories that are now empty. Its warnings explain the `A--B` + `C` versus `A` + `B--C` slug collapse. |
| `src/runner.rs:392-413` `finish_library_write` | Removes the album staging directory after the album has been written to the library. |

## Goal

A completed download stages under `<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/`, for every mode, with
both components produced by the same sanitiser the library write uses, and with no
behaviour change anywhere else: same recovery semantics, same cleanup, same database keys.

## Scope

### In scope

- The staging path layout and every site that builds or decodes it.
- A startup migration for staging directories left by earlier versions.
- The recovery scan's album-identity lookup, which the new layout and the sanitiser change.
- Cleanup of the artist level when an album leaves staging.
- An audit that records, and tests that enforce, one sanitiser for every folder seakarr
  creates.

### Out of scope

- The library layout, which is already `<library root>/<artist>/<album>/` and does not change.
- Placement semantics: placement still never creates an artist folder, and still writes only

`downloads/staging/Artist Name/Album Name/01 - Track.flac`.

The flattened name is not only cosmetic. It is a lossy encoding of two values into one
path component, and the code that consumes it has to decode it again:

| Site | Behaviour today |
| --- | --- |
| `src/runner.rs:508-516` | Builds `format!("{}--{}", artist.replace(['/','\\'], "-"), album.unwrap_or("unknown").replace(['/','\\'], "-"))` and joins it to the staging root. |
| `src/organizer.rs:516-533` `disc_subdir` | Walks a staged file's parent directories and stops when a directory name `.contains("--")`, because that names the album staging root. An album whose own name contains `--` cannot be told from a boundary by this test. |
| `src/organizer.rs:758-763` `parse_album_slug` | Splits on the first `--` to recover `(artist, album)`; a name without a separator becomes album `"Unknown"`. |
| `src/organizer.rs:774-810` `recover_interrupted_upgrades` | Reads the top level of the staging root, treats every directory as an album slug, re-verifies a `success` album by copying it back, and deletes every other leftover. |

| `src/runner.rs:392-413` `finish_library_write` | Removes the album staging directory after the album has been written to the library. |

## Goal

A completed download stages under `<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/`, for every mode, with
both components produced by the same sanitiser the library write uses, and with no
behaviour change anywhere else: same recovery semantics, same cleanup, same database keys.

## Scope

### In scope

- The staging path layout and every site that builds or decodes it.
- A startup migration for staging directories left by earlier versions.
- The recovery scan's album-identity lookup, which the new layout and the sanitiser change.
- Cleanup of the artist level when an album leaves staging.
- An audit that records, and tests that enforce, one sanitiser for every folder seakarr
  creates.

### Out of scope

- The library layout, which is already `<library root>/<artist>/<album>/` and does not change.
- Placement semantics: placement still never creates an artist folder, and still writes only
  into an artist folder the library already holds.
- Any new or changed configuration key. `storage.staging_dir` keeps its meaning and default
  (`downloads/staging`).
- A validation that `storage.staging_dir` sits outside every `library.paths` entry. The
  README documents the requirement; this change does not add a gate.
- Disc subdirectory nesting inside an album (`download.rs`), which is unchanged because it
  receives the finished album path.
- Historical design documents that record the old layout
  (`docs/agent/specs/2026-09-15-discover-library-placement-design.md:14`,
  `docs/agent/specs/2026-09-23-remove-organize-design.md:209`). They are dated records and
  are left as written.

## Decisions

### Staging albums are two path components

`<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/`. The artist level exists for every album, including an
album-only manual run, which names no artist. That keeps one rule, and therefore one
recovery walk, instead of a layout whose depth depends on which request produced it.

### Both components use `sanitize_component`

The artist component and the album component each pass through
`organizer::sanitize_component`, the function every library write already uses: Windows
reserved characters and control characters are removed, a trailing dot or space is trimmed,
a reserved device name is prefixed (`CON` becomes `_CON`), and a value that sanitises to
nothing becomes `_`.

Consequences, all deliberate:

- The staging tree mirrors the library tree for the same album, so a folder name that
  renders correctly in the library renders correctly in staging too.
- An album-only run (blank artist) stages under the `_` placeholder:
  `<staging_dir>/_/<album>/`. `_` is the sanitiser's existing placeholder for "this value
  keeps nothing", and `ArtistFolderIndex` already refuses to treat `_` as an artist folder
  (`src/discover.rs:319-320`), so the placeholder cannot be mistaken for a library match.
- An artist-only run that names no album keeps today's `"unknown"` album component:
  `<staging_dir>/<artist>/unknown/`.

### A new `src/staging.rs` owns the layout

The layout rule, the migration, and the staging scan move into one small module. This
follows the crate's existing idiom (`discs.rs`, `tracks.rs`, `report.rs`) and keeps the two
riskiest behaviours of this change — a merge that must never overwrite, and a name lookup
that must resolve a sanitised directory back to a raw album — unit-testable without a
runner, a client, or a download.

`organizer.rs` keeps the library half of recovery (`resume_library_upgrade`) and the
sanitiser. `runner.rs` keeps orchestration and calls into the module.

### Legacy `<artist>--<album>` folders are migrated at startup

`normalise_layout` runs once per run, before the recovery scan, and is **not** gated on
`library_upgrade.enabled`: the layout rule belongs to staging, not to one mode. It renames
each top-level `<artist>--<album>` directory into the nested form, so a leftover from an
earlier version is still found by the recovery scan and by the operator.

`parse_album_slug` is kept, renamed in documentation as the legacy parser, and used only by
the migration. It is removed from the recovery path.

### Migration merges without overwriting

Migrating a legacy directory whose nested destination already exists must not destroy
either copy:

- Rename each entry that is absent at the destination, recursing into subdirectories so a
  legacy `CD 01/` folder keeps its shape.
- When a name already exists at the destination, keep the destination file and leave the
  legacy copy where it is. Nothing is overwritten.
- A legacy directory that the merge emptied is removed. A legacy directory that still holds
  a skipped entry is left in place and reported, naming the first entry that stopped it —
  the same shape of warning `discard_refused_staging` already emits.

### Recovery resolves identity by a sanitised match

`recover_interrupted_upgrades` identifies an album by looking a directory name up in the
`processed_albums` table, which stores raw names (`db.get_album_status`). With sanitised
directory names, an exact lookup would miss (`Gold: Greatest Hits` stages as
`Gold_ Greatest Hits`), and a missed lookup means the leftover is deleted as untracked
debris — data loss for an interrupted upgrade that was about to be recovered.

`staging::scan` therefore loads `db.get_processed_albums()` once and matches each
`<artist>/<album>` directory against rows by comparing `sanitize_component(row.artist)` and
`sanitize_component(row.album)` with the two directory names, case-insensitively. A match
yields the row's **raw** names and status, which are what `resume_library_upgrade` needs:
it sanitises them again for the library destination (sanitising is idempotent, so the
destination is unchanged) and the status write keeps the raw key. No row yields no
identity, and the leftover is cleaned exactly as today.

When several rows match, the highest `id` wins and the ambiguity is warned about, so the
most recently tried album is the one recovered.

### `disc_subdir` stops at the album root by name, not by a separator

`disc_subdir` currently stops walking when a parent directory name contains `--`. It is
called from exactly one place, `organizer.rs:426` inside `copy_into_library`, where the
album string is already in scope, so it instead stops when the directory name equals
`sanitize_component(album)` — the album staging directory's own name. This is the same
boundary without the separator sniff, and the innermost-match-first walk still returns a
real disc folder before it reaches the album root, so a multi-disc album whose own name
carries an embedded disc marker (`Gold (Disc 1)`) behaves as it does today.

### An empty artist directory is pruned

The artist level is a directory seakarr creates, so it is removed when it holds nothing:

- Immediately, by `finish_library_write` and `discard_refused_staging`, once the album
  directory they handle has gone.
- Elsewhere, by `normalise_layout` at the start of the next run, which removes an artist
  directory that holds no entries at all. This covers a failure path that removed an album
  directory and left its parent behind.

`fs::remove_dir` refuses a non-empty directory, so an artist's second album, staged
concurrently or left from an interrupted run, can never be removed by this.

### Sanitisation is consistent across every library write

One rule, one function: every production path that turns an artist or album string into a
path component calls `sanitize_component` at the moment the name is created. There is no
second sanitiser and no per-mode variant. Staging joins that set.

The audit below records the state this change must preserve, so a later reader can tell a
deliberate exception from an oversight:

| Library-write path | Artist component | Album and file components |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy_to_library` (`organizer.rs:328` → `library_relative_path:129-134`) | `sanitize_component(artist)` | `sanitize_component(album/track/title/ext)` |
| `place_into_library` (`album_dir_for:145-158`) | the existing on-disk folder name, used **verbatim** | `sanitize_component(album)` |
| `delete_lesser_quality_files:545-554` | sanitised | sanitised |
| `resume_library_upgrade:696-698`, per-entry leaf `:723`/`:728` | sanitised | sanitised |
| `disc_subdir:531` (a disc label becomes a real folder) | n/a | sanitised |
| `search.rs:1211-1256`, `discover.rs:319-320` (lookups, both sides) | sanitised | sanitised |
| staged file names (`download.rs`) | n/a | peer basename, `safe_basename`-checked; never a library folder |

The single exception is `place_into_library`, and it is deliberate: its `artist_dir` is the
name of an artist folder that already exists on disk, found by the library walk or
`ArtistFolderIndex`, and placement exists to write *into* that folder rather than create a
differently-named one beside it. Re-sanitising it would not add safety — `album_dir_for`
already rejects any value that is not a single ordinary path component — it would split one
artist across two folders. Every folder seakarr *creates* comes from a sanitised name.
