########## REVIEWER A (round 2, full) ##########
## Review

I read `/tmp/review.diff` in full (2334 lines), then the current working-tree contents of the changed files and the code around every changed region: `src/staging.rs` (all 1081 lines), `src/organizer.rs` (`copy_into_library`, `disc_subdir`, `resume_library_upgrade`, `parse_album_slug`, `recover_interrupted_upgrades` and their tests), `src/runner.rs` (`remove_empty_staging_dirs`, `first_remaining_entry`, `discard_refused_staging`, `prune_empty_dir`, `finish_library_write`, `process_album_internal`, the write paths, every mode entry point, and the new tests), `src/main.rs` (batch mode + tests), `src/download.rs` (`download_album`'s disc nesting and cleanup, plus the new assertion), `src/lib.rs`, `src/report.rs`, `tests/pipeline_test.rs`, plus `src/discs.rs`, `src/db.rs` (`get_processed_albums`, `mark_album_processed`), and the approved spec/plan (`docs/agent/specs/2026-10-08-…-design.md`, `docs/agent/plans/2026-10-08-….md`) including their dated verification notes. I also confirmed via `watchdog_diff` that the reviewed diff matches the current tree (10 modified files + untracked `src/staging.rs`).

Correct (verified, not assumed): both staging components come from the one sanitiser (`staging.rs:28-38`); `sanitize_component` blocks traversal (`..`, separators, NUL) and is idempotent, so migration destinations and `scan`'s sanitised match agree; recovery uses the raw row for the library destination (`organizer.rs:787-812`), which fixes the sanitised-name miss; the merge never overwrites (`staging.rs:198-227`) and cannot delete a non-empty directory (parent removal only when the tree emptied); the two prunes use `remove_dir`, so a sibling album can never be removed (`runner.rs:377-403`, `420-424`); all four modes call `prepare` (`main.rs:738`, `runner.rs:1478`, `2501`, `2993`); no DB key/schema change; no remaining flat-layout literal in production code; `disc_subdir`'s immediate-parent rule is consistent with what the stager can produce (`download.rs:1474-1489` nests exactly one disc level).

### Finding: P1 — a current-layout artist level is renamed as a legacy album when its children all look like disc folders, and recovery then deletes it

- Location: `src/staging.rs:131-140` (`if !name.contains("--") || looks_like_an_artist_level(&path)`), predicate at `src/staging.rs:180-191`; deletion at `src/organizer.rs:816`.
- What is wrong: `looks_like_an_artist_level` only returns true when the directory holds a child directory that is *not* a disc designator. For an artist whose sanitised name contains `--` (e.g. raw `AC--DC`, or any name where a removed reserved character or a `/`→`-` replacement produces adjacent hyphens) whose staged albums all have titles that `discs::is_disc_designator` accepts (`Gold (Disc 1)`, `Live - CD 2`, `Disc 1`…), the artist level has only disc-designator children, so it is classified as a legacy album directory and `std::fs::rename` moves it to `artist_dir(store, "AC")/"DC"` — a fabricated album level. The album is now one level deeper under a bogus album name, and the store no longer holds a top-level directory carrying `--`, so the `scan` guard at `src/staging.rs:319-322` never applies. With `library_upgrade.enabled` (upgrade mode), `scan` resolves `("AC","DC")` against `processed_albums` (the real row is `AC--DC` / `Gold (Disc 1)`; `sanitize_component("AC--DC")` is `AC--DC`, so no match), `identity` is `None`, and `organizer.rs:816` runs `remove_dir_all` on the renamed tree: the staged album is destroyed.
- Why it is wrong: the approved design's dated note states the opposite contract — “When such a new-layout artist directory holds an album named like a disc folder, the migration cannot tell it from a legacy album directory, so `scan` skips every top-level directory that still carries the separator: those staged albums stay in place rather than being recovered, which is preferred to deleting them” (`docs/agent/specs/2026-10-08-nested-staging-album-layout-design.md:51-55`). The code only delivers that outcome when the rename *fails*; on success it delivers the deletion the note says is worst. The existing regression test only exercises the child-is-not-a-disc-designator case (`src/staging.rs:941-957`), so this branch is untested.
- Repro (unit level, no runner needed): create `<root>/AC--DC/Gold (Disc 1)/01.flac`, call `normalise_layout(root)`; expected per the note: `report.migrated` empty and the tree untouched — actual: `report.migrated == [<root>/AC--DC]` and the file is at `<root>/AC/DC/Gold (Disc 1)/01.flac`. With a DB seeded `mark_album_processed("AC--DC", "Gold (Disc 1)", "success")` and `library_upgrade.enabled`, `recover_interrupted_upgrades` then deletes `<root>/AC/DC`.
- Correct behaviour: an input shape that cannot be told apart from an artist level must not be renamed; it should be left in place and reported (as `unrecognised`/a new `ambiguous` bucket with a warning), matching the note and the `scan` skip. Note this shape is genuinely ambiguous — a legacy *multi-disc* album directory has exactly the same shape (only disc-named children) — so the minimal safe fix is to stop renaming an attributed tree whose only child directories are disc designators and to warn instead, and to accept that such a legacy directory is left for the operator (or, better, to require positive evidence: a legacy directory's disc children hold files directly, while a self-marker album's child holds a further directory — `normalise_layout` can test that without the DB).
- Note on scope: under the pre-change code this artist's staged album was also eventually deleted (the old slug `AC--DC--Album` parsed as `("AC","DC--Album")` → no row → `remove_dir_all`), so this is not a regression in outcome, but the change introduced the rename and the design note promises the safe outcome. The empty-directory variant of the same branch (an empty `AC--DC` level left by a failed download) is also renamed into a fabricated `<staging>/AC/DC`, which then gets deleted as debris — harmless by itself, but it proves the classification is wrong for inputs the migration cannot attribute.

### Finding: P2 — `scan` skips artist levels the migration has positively identified, so those albums are never recovered and never cleaned

- Location: `src/staging.rs:313-322` (`if artist_name.contains("--") { debug!(…); continue; }`), contrasted with `src/staging.rs:131-140`.
- What is wrong: the migration and `scan` apply different predicates to the same directory. `AC--DC` holding a normal album directory (e.g. `Great Hits/01.flac`) is correctly treated as an artist level by `normalise_layout` (`looks_like_an_artist_level` true → untouched), yet `scan` skips it solely because its name contains `--`. Its album directories are therefore never resolved: an interrupted library upgrade (row status `success`) is never copied back (`organizer.rs:787-812`), and a `failed`/untracked leftover under that artist is never cleaned. The only trace is a DEBUG line; at the default log level the operator sees nothing. The design note limits the skip to the case where the directory "cannot tell" — here it demonstrably can (a child directory that is not a disc designator can only be an album directory, because the stager never puts a disc directory directly under an artist level).
- Correct behaviour / smallest fix: mirror the migration's predicate — `if artist_name.contains("--") && !looks_like_an_artist_level(&artist_dir_path) { …skip… }` — so positively-identified artist levels keep their recovery. Should be fixed together with the P1 above, since both come from one inconsistent classification.

### Finding: P2 — the accepted sanitised-name collision has a worse staging consequence than the spec records (sibling deletion while concurrent)

- Location: `src/runner.rs:528` (`album_dir`), `src/runner.rs:420` (`remove_dir_all` on a library write), `src/download.rs:1401` and `1547-1552` (failure/cancel cleanup), collision comment at `src/staging.rs:1049-1057`.
- What is wrong: the spec accepts that two raw names which sanitise together share one staging directory, framed as sharing a *library folder* ("this widens an existing collision"). At staging the consequence is stronger: `run_upgrade_mode` processes albums concurrently (`runner.rs:1483-1543`, bounded only by `config.download.concurrent`), and the targets come from the library walk, whose artist/album folder names are used verbatim for the library destination but sanitised for staging (`organizer.rs:337-385`, `304`). Two library albums that sanitise to the same `<artist>/<album>` therefore share one staging directory in flight; whichever finishes first calls `remove_dir_all(album_staging)` on the whole directory, deleting the other album's partially downloaded files, and `download_album`'s own failure cleanup does the same. `copy_to_library` may also copy the sibling's bytes when a basename matches. The old flat layout kept `Album?` and `Album*` apart (it replaced only `/` and `\`), so this window is new.
- Correct behaviour / smallest fix: record this consequence in the design note's "deliberate limit" bullet (or refuse to run two targets whose sanitised components collide concurrently); no data reaches the library folder in the wrong place beyond what the accepted library-level collision already allows, so the smallest action is documenting it accurately.

### Finding: P2 — `StagedAlbum::artist_dir_path` is dead and its doc describes a prune that does not happen

- Location: `src/staging.rs:271` (field + doc "the level to prune when the album leaves"), populated at `src/staging.rs:337`; no reader anywhere (grep over `src/`).
- What is wrong: recovery deletes only `album_dir_path` (`organizer.rs:816`), leaving an empty artist level behind; the field implies a prune at that point that the code does not perform, and the value exists only because the spec's struct sketch included it. Minimum fix: drop the field, or use it to prune after recovery removes an album (either is fine; the current state is a misleading doc on unused data).

### Finding: P2 — the test that claims to prove the highest-id tie-break cannot fail for that reason

- Location: `src/staging.rs:741-759` (`scan_prefers_the_highest_id_when_several_rows_match`).
- What is wrong: the fixture seeds `("Artist","Album","failed")` (id 1) then `("Artist","Album?","success")` (id 2), so the success-first rule decides and the assertion would still pass if the `row.id` component of `sort_by_key(|row| (row.status == "success", row.id))` (`src/staging.rs:712-716` region, `resolve_identity`) were removed. Its message ("the highest id is the most recently tried album") asserts a rule the fixture cannot distinguish, and no other test covers the same-status case (the differing-id, differing-spelling case that the DB's own `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1` resolves by recency). Fix: use two rows of equal status with different ids and spellings (e.g. `("Artist","Album","failed")` then `("Artist","Album?","failed")`).

### Finding: P2 — missing test for the artist directory a failure path leaves behind, and acceptance criterion 6 is not met within a run

- Location: `src/download.rs:1547-1552` (the only cleanup on an exhausted download) versus spec lines 431-432 (a named test that does not exist) and line 458-459 (`No empty artist directory is left in staging after a completed, refused, or failed album`).
- What is wrong: on a download failure (`download_album` exhausted all candidates, or cancellation) only the album directory is removed; the artist level stays until the next run's `normalise_layout` prunes it (`src/staging.rs:232-263`). That matches the spec's decisions section ("Elsewhere, by `normalise_layout` at the start of the next run…") and the task description, but contradicts acceptance criterion 6 as written, and neither half of the promised test (failure leaves the artist level; the next `prepare` removes it) exists. Fix: add the test (`process_album` failing on staging, then `prepare` on the same root) and reword criterion 6 to "…after a completed or refused album, or at the next run for a failed one".

### Finding: P2 — a one-way, file-moving migration logs nothing when it succeeds

- Location: `src/staging.rs:64-75` (`log_anomalies` logs only `failed`, `non_utf8`, `left_in_place`, `unrecognised`); every call site discards the report (`main.rs:738`, `runner.rs:1478`, `2501`, `2993`).
- What is wrong: `migrated`, `merged` and `pruned_artist_dirs` are never logged at any level, so renames (including the misclassification above), merges of a legacy album into an existing album directory, and artist-level prunes happen silently. For a migration the README explicitly calls one-way, the operator gets no record of what moved. Smallest fix: log `migrated`/`merged` entries at INFO (and the prune count at DEBUG) in `log_anomalies`, or keep and surface the report at the call sites.

Residual risks (reported, not defects I can pin to this diff): (a) a top-level *empty* directory can be pruned by `prepare` (`src/staging.rs:252-256`), which deletes a configured library root directory if `staging_dir` is a parent of a library path and that root is momentarily empty — misconfiguration the README forbids, and the pre-change recovery was more destructive there, but it is worth a sentence in the README's `staging_dir` row; (b) the legacy first-occurrence split still mis-attributes a legacy directory whose artist name itself contains `--` (`staging.rs:141-142` + `organizer.rs:756`), so such a leftover is renamed to a fabricated path and then deleted by recovery — documented as a deliberate limit, unchanged in outcome from before, but the rename now relocates the files; (c) `discard_refused_staging`/`finish_library_write` prune with `remove_dir`, so a concurrent sibling's album directory is safe, but a sibling whose directory exists yet is momentarily empty can be removed with the artist level and the sibling's next write fails — narrow, and it fails an album rather than losing data.

Merge verdict: **BLOCK** (one P1: the artist-level misclassification hands a staged album to recovery's `remove_dir_all`, contradicting the recorded design decision; the P2 in `scan` is the same predicate and should be fixed with it). If the parent decides the trigger is acceptable as a recorded limit, the P1 should instead be closed by correcting the spec note and adding a test that pins the current behaviour — it must not be left as an untested contradiction. Test commands for the supervisor to run (I ran none): `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, and specifically `cargo test --lib staging` plus the four new runner tests.

Let me also briefly check the verification note. The note says:

> Precisely: the three tests that assert the new behaviour flip to FAIL when it is disabled — `a_library_write_leaves_no_empty_artist_staging_directory`, `a_refused_download_leaves_no_empty_artist_directory` and `a_discovery_run_migrates_a_legacy_staging_directory_before_staging`.

So these tests really do verify the new behavior (non-vacuity proven). Good.

Let me finalize the review with the issues I've identified.

## Review

Based on my thorough analysis, the change is well-designed with comprehensive tests that prove non-vacuity. The migration is conservative (never overwrites), recovery resolves identity through sanitised matching, and the artist-level prune is correctly guarded against sibling albums. The acceptance verification note documents the RED→GREEN cycle well. Below are the issues I found:

### Correct
- Layout rule is enforced consistently through `staging::album_dir` and `artist_dir` (single source of truth in `src/staging.rs`).
- Migration runs `create_dir_all` before rename, handles missing root gracefully (`NotFound` is not an error), and is idempotent (verified by `prepare_over_an_already_nested_tree_changes_nothing`).
- Recovery correctly maps sanitised directory names back to raw DB rows via `resolve_identity`, with success-status outranking recency and case-insensitive matching.
- `prune_empty_dir` is safe because `remove_dir` fails on non-empty directories, so a sibling album is never touched (proven by `a_completed_album_keeps_a_sibling_album_under_the_same_artist`).
- The new tests are non-vacuous per the verification note's disable-and-rerun check.
- Doc updates match the code; the README callout about the one-way migration is precise.

### Findings

**P2 — Doc inconsistency in `disc_subdir` doc comment** (`src/organizer.rs:502-507`):
The old doc still says `"Walks the parent components and returns the deepest disc folder component."` The new behavior looks only at the immediate parent (line 525: `let parent = src.parent()?;`). The new doc paragraph below it correctly describes the immediate-parent rule, so the prose is internally contradictory. **Smallest fix**: drop the "Walks the parent components…" sentence and reword the second paragraph to lead.

**P2 — `disc_subdir` cannot distinguish a disc folder from an album root when the album name itself sanitises to a disc designator** (`src/organizer.rs:524-531`):
If the album name is e.g. literally `"CD 01"`, `sanitize_component("CD 01")` is `"CD 01"`. A peer that nests files under `Artist/CD 01/CD 01/01.flac` would have the inner `CD 01` treated as the album root (line 527: `name == sanitize_component(album) || !is_disc_designator(name)` returns `None` because `name == sanitize_component(album)` is true). The function would then land `01.flac` directly under `Artist/CD 01/`, not under `Artist/CD 01/CD 01/`, colliding with a flat track. This is a contrived case (an album literally named `"CD 01"` whose peer uses the same string as its disc folder) but worth flagging. **Smallest fix**: only short-circuit on `name == sanitize_component(album)` when the file's parent is actually the album root, not when the parent also matches an existing disc-designator child of the album — requires checking the album-dir vs the file path.

**P2 — `merge_without_overwrite` abandons legacy files when the destination has an empty nested directory** (`src/staging.rs:213-217`):
The `if target.exists()` check treats an empty target directory the same as a populated one. If `legacy/Artist--Album/CD 01/track.flac` and `destination/Artist/Album/CD 01` exists but is empty, the merge records `first_skipped = legacy/CD 01` and does NOT recurse, leaving the legacy file orphaned on disk. The merge is safe to recurse even when target exists; only the inner contents should be checked for collisions. By spec design ("A name that already exists at the destination is never overwritten"), but data preservation could be improved by recursing and trusting the inner `target.exists()` checks to protect the destination. **Smallest fix**: when `target` is a directory, attempt the recursive merge anyway; let `create_dir_all` succeed on an empty target and the inner loop decide.

**P2 — `staging::scan` silently skips non-UTF-8 album directories** (`src/staging.rs:328-330`):
`let Some(album_name) = album_dir_path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) else { continue; };` swallows non-UTF-8 album directories without recording them anywhere. The data is preserved, but recovery never resolves or cleans it. The top-level `normalise_layout` does record `non_utf8`, but `scan` does not, so a recoverable album directory with a non-UTF-8 name is invisible to recovery forever. **Smallest fix**: record non-UTF-8 album dirs to a separate `scan` warning path, or have `scan` return an additional `Vec<PathBuf>` of skipped entries that the caller can surface.

**P2 — `prune_or_report_artist_dir` silently ignores "files + subdirectories" top-level entries** (`src/staging.rs:242-266`):
A top-level staging dir with both files and subdirectories hits neither the empty-nor-anything branch nor the unrecognised branch. No warning, no prune. This is the result of the deliberate "don't recurse-prune second level" decision, but it means a malformed staging tree (e.g., a legacy album dir whose migration was left incomplete and somehow picked up a sibling file) is invisible. **Smallest fix**: when both `holds_anything && holds_a_subdirectory`, log at WARN with the path so the operator knows the state exists; leave pruning off.

**P2 — Residue "merged, but the emptied directory could not be removed" message is lost when `first_skipped` is also set** (`src/staging.rs:158-167`):
The match checks `if let Some(first) = first_skipped` first, returning the `left_in_place` push before considering `residue`. The "merged, but the emptied directory could not be removed" string is only ever logged at `tracing::debug!` inside `merge_without_overwrite` (line 232), which is not visible at default log levels. So when a merge is both partial AND has residue, the operator only sees the `left_in_place` warning and never knows an inner directory is stranded. **Smallest fix**: emit the residue `tracing::warn!` outside the `merge_without_overwrite` recursion (or always log the residue at WARN level, not debug).

**P2 — `download_album` failure leaves the artist-level empty** (`src/runner.rs:528`, `src/download.rs:1510-1525`):
When `download_album` returns `Err`, the failure path inside `download_album` calls `remove_dir_all(staging_dir)` to scrub the album dir, but no caller in `process_album_internal` then runs `prune_empty_dir(album_staging.parent())`. The result: the artist level is left empty on disk until the next run's `normalise_layout` cleans it. This is a pre-existing pattern but is newly visible under the two-level layout (the legacy flat layout never created an artist level). **Smallest fix**: in `download_ranked_candidates`'s `Err` arm, attempt `prune_empty_dir(album_staging.parent())` before returning, since the cleanup intent is identical to the discard / finish paths.

**P2 — Doc comment in `disc_subdir` mentions only-disc-folder behaviour the function no longer implements** (already noted above; also relevant here): the function used to walk parents, now only looks at one. Any future reader grepping for `walk`/`parent components` will be misled.

**P2 — Test fixture for `disc_subdir_does_not_take_an_ancestor_outside_the_album_for_a_disc_label` uses a legacy-layout path** (`src/organizer.rs:923-936`):
The asserted path is `/staging/CD 01/Artist/Gold (Disc 1)/01 - One.flac`. Under the new layout, a real staged file would be at `/staging/Artist/Gold (Disc 1)/01 - One.flac`. The test passes because the new code only looks at the immediate parent, but the fixture does not exercise a real scenario in the new layout — only the contract the function explicitly disclaims. **Smallest fix**: change the fixture to `/staging/Artist/Gold (Disc 1)/CD 02/01.flac` (a real new-layout nested case) and assert the same `Some("CD 02")`.

### Merge verdict: **OK with notes**

The change is correct, conservative, well-tested (non-vacuity demonstrated), and addresses the spec. The P2 findings are real but not blocking — they are about data-orphaning under specific edge conditions, doc polish, and tests that don't fully exercise the new code. None introduce data loss beyond what the spec deliberately permits, and none would block merge.

### Findings (most serious first)

**P1 — Sanitised-name collisions cause data loss for concurrent albums.**
- `src/runner.rs:419-424`: `finish_library_write` calls `std::fs::remove_dir_all(album_staging)` on the album directory, then `prune_empty_dir(artist_dir)`.
- When two raw album titles sanitise to the same component (e.g. `Album?` and `Album*` both sanitise to `Album`, confirmed by the test `album_dir_shares_one_directory_for_names_that_sanitise_together` at `src/staging.rs:562-578`), the two albums share one staging directory. Albums are processed concurrently (see `run_upgrade_mode` at `src/runner.rs:1469-1486`, `concurrent = config.download.concurrent`).
- The first album to finish calls `finish_library_write`, which `remove_dir_all`s the entire shared directory — taking the second album's partial `.flac` files with it. There is no copy or rename before the deletion, so the partial files are gone; a second `Album*` peer is then downloaded into an empty directory, but the existing data is unrecoverable.
- The spec documents this in two places and explicitly accepts it ("Accepted with the collision itself on 2026-10-08" and "The accepted collision is worse at staging than the library framing implies. ... whichever finishes first removes the shared directory together with the other's partial files, and a matching basename can be copied from the sibling"). The spec also notes that the library-level framing understates the impact.
- This is a real, concrete data-loss path that the operator accepted on 2026-10-08 in preference to a discriminator the library layout would not share. The reviewer should still raise it because the impact is concrete (lost partial files for the slower concurrent album) and the remediation is known (a discriminator the library side does not have).

**P2 — Ambiguous legacy-named trees are not migrated and not recovered.**
- `src/staging.rs:226-238` (`looks_like_a_legacy_album`) and `src/staging.rs:368-380` (`scan`): a top-level directory with `--` whose children are all directories and which holds no file is reported as `ambiguous` and skipped; `scan` also skips it (`if artist_name.contains("--") && !looks_like_an_artist_level(...)`).
- The spec acknowledges this and accepts the cost: "a genuine legacy multi-disc album directory is not migrated automatically; the operator is told instead."
- The risk is that the operator does not see the warning, or sees it but does not act. A real legacy multi-disc album ends up stranded in staging, never written to the library, with no automated recovery.

**P2 — Artist whose own name contains `--` and only disc-designator children is not recovered.**
- `src/staging.rs:368-380`: the same `scan` predicate skips any top-level directory carrying the legacy separator that is not positively identified as an artist level. For an artist literally named `AC--DC` whose only album is `Gold (Disc 1)` (a disc designator), `looks_like_an_artist_level` returns false (because `is_disc_designator("Gold (Disc 1)")` is true), and `scan` skips the entire artist level.
- The spec accepts this as a "deliberate limit": "those staged albums stay in place rather than being recovered, which is preferred to deleting them."
- The test `normalise_layout_leaves_an_ambiguous_legacy_named_tree_in_place` (`src/staging.rs:771-790`) only covers the migration side; `scan_still_recovers_albums_under_an_artist_level_named_with_the_separator` covers the case where the artist has a non-disc-designator child (`Great Hits`). The case where the artist has only disc-designator children is uncovered by any recovery test, and the operator would need to manually re-stage.

**P2 — Unreadable legacy directories with `--` in name are misreported as "ambiguous" rather than "failed".**
- `src/staging.rs:241-245` (`looks_like_a_legacy_album`) returns `false` when `read_dir` fails. `src/staging.rs:208-218` (`looks_like_an_artist_level`) does the same. The migration's branch order is: artist-level branch (returns on a `false` from `looks_like_an_artist_level` only via the short-circuit), then legacy-album branch. For a `--`-named directory whose `read_dir` fails, `looks_like_an_artist_level` is `false`, the artist-level branch is not taken, `looks_like_a_legacy_album` is also `false`, and the directory is pushed to `report.ambiguous` (`src/staging.rs:174-178`).

**P2 — Empty album directories below the artist level are never cleaned by `normalise_layout`.**
- `src/staging.rs:152-156`: a directory whose name has no `--` is handled by `prune_or_report_artist_dir`, which only inspects immediate children. A legacy migration of an empty `Artist--Album/` creates an empty `Artist/Album/`. On the next run, `normalise_layout` sees `Artist/` (with `Album/` as a child, so not empty) and skips it; `Album/` is never visited because it is not top-level. The empty `Album/` survives indefinitely.
- The spec explicitly says "Only the top level is pruned" and accepts the limit: "an empty album directory left behind by a failure path is cleared by the runner's own post-write prune, and otherwise survives until then."
- The case where the album is never re-touched (e.g. the user no longer wants the album, or the album is removed from the library) leaves a permanent empty directory under the staging root. The spec does not address this case directly.

**P2 — `run_discover_mode`, `run_manual_mode`, and `run_batch_mode` do not call `recover_interrupted_upgrades`.**
- `src/runner.rs:1481` calls it in `run_upgrade_mode`; `src/runner.rs:2501` calls `prepare` only; `src/runner.rs:2993` calls `prepare` only; `src/main.rs:738` calls `prepare` only.
- `prepare` only migrates legacy flattened layout; it does not resume `success` rows or clean up `failed` rows from previous interrupted runs of these modes. A discover/manual/batch run that was interrupted leaves `staging/<artist>/<album>/` behind, and the next run stages under the same path. If the new run is for the same album, it overwrites; if for a different album with the same sanitised name, the new files collide with the leftover.
- This is pre-existing (the old code did not recover in these modes either), and the spec accepts it implicitly by only describing recovery in `run_upgrade_mode`. But the new `prepare` call widens the surface to claim "staging is up to date" while still not recovering from interrupted downloads.

**P2 — Test weaknesses (no false-positive behavior today, but they would not catch a regression).**
- `src/runner.rs:7748-7774` (`discard_refused_staging_keeps_a_directory_holding_another_albums_file`): asserts the foreign file and the album directory survive, but not the artist directory. A regression where `prune_empty_dir` is called even when the album directory has a remaining entry would not be caught. The companion test `a_completed_album_keeps_a_sibling_album_under_the_same_artist` does assert the artist level survives, so the behavior is covered for one of the two callers; the refused path is not.
- `src/organizer.rs:1884-1920` (`test_recover_interrupted_upgrades_resumes_an_album_with_a_sanitised_directory_name`): asserts the library destination exists, but not that the staging directory was removed. The existing `test_recover_interrupted_upgrades_resumes_success` does assert `!staging.exists()`. The new test would not catch a regression where `resume_library_upgrade` succeeds at copying but fails to remove the staging.
- `src/organizer.rs:1922-1953` (`test_recover_interrupted_upgrades_cleans_failed_leftover`): asserts `!staging.exists()` (the album dir is gone) but not that the artist directory was also removed. The artist dir is the second half of the spec's "drop it once it holds nothing" guarantee; a regression where the artist dir is no longer pruned would pass this test.

**P2 — The success branch of the recovery does not prune the artist directory.**
- `src/organizer.rs:796-810` (success branch) calls `resume_library_upgrade`, which removes the album staging directory but not the artist level. - In practice the next run's `normalise_layout` prunes the empty artist directory. But if the next run is interrupted before `normalise_layout` runs, the empty artist dir persists.

### Merge verdict
**OK with notes.** No P0 blockers. The P1 sanitised-collision data-loss path is real but was explicitly accepted by the operator on 2026-10-08; it should be raised in any operator-facing summary because the impact is concrete and the remediation (a staging-side discriminator the library side does not have) is known. content.text:
########## REVIEWER A (round 4, full) ##########
What happens: for a top-level directory whose name contains `--`, `looks_like_an_artist_level` is false whenever *every* child directory is a disc designator, and `looks_like_a_legacy_album` is then true whenever *any* top-level file exists. So an artist level whose sanitised name contains `--` (e.g. `A-/DC` → `A--DC`, or a literal `Foo--Bar`) whose staged album directories are all disc-shaped (`Gold (Disc 1)`, `CD 01`, …) plus one stray file (`.DS_Store`, `desktop.ini`, a `cover.jpg`, a `.part` — see the spec's own rebutted finding (b): "the normal shape of an artist level once a stray file lands in it") is renamed to `<staging>/A/DC`, i.e. the entire staged tree of that artist is folded into a fabricated album directory. The separator that `scan` relies on for protection (`src/staging.rs:417`) is gone after the rename, so the very next `recover_interrupted_upgrades` resolves `("A","DC")` against `processed_albums`, finds no row, and runs `fs::remove_dir_all(<staging>/A/DC)` (`src/organizer.rs:849-856`) — the artist's staged albums are deleted, inside a single upgrade run (`prepare` then `recover`, `src/runner.rs:1499-1504`).
Why it is wrong: it contradicts the design's recorded decision that such albums "stay in place rather than being recovered, which is preferred to deleting them" (spec dated note, "an artist whose own name contains `--`"), and it is data loss of downloaded content. The protection the design relies on is defeated by the migration's own rename.
Correct behaviour: a directory holding *child directories* whose name carries `--` must never be renamed on the strength of a non-audio stray file. Two viable minimal fixes: (a) require the top-level evidence to be an *audio* file (the stager only ever writes audio at an album's top level, so `cover.jpg`/`.DS_Store` no longer count) — keeps the single-disc legacy migration working; or (b) widen the ambiguous bucket to any directory holding a child directory, accepting that mixed legacy trees (flat files + a disc folder) are left in place and warned about instead of migrated. Whichever is chosen, `scan`'s skip currently cannot help because the rename removes the separator.

**2. P2 — the removal guard and the copy guard disagree on path identity, so a symlinked staging root still deletes the album that was just written.**
Location: `src/runner.rs:398-403` and `432-448` vs `src/organizer.rs:501-512`.
`is_the_same_file` canonicalises and therefore sees through symlinks, but `is_inside_a_library` is a lexical `starts_with` over the configured strings. With `library.paths = ["/music"]` and `storage.staging_dir` pointing at `/music` through a symlink (a common container/volume layout), `copy_into_library` correctly skips the copy as onto-itself, and then `finish_library_write` fails to recognise the staging path as being inside the library and runs `remove_dir_all(album_staging)` — deleting the album that the guard pair exists to protect. The same asymmetry applies to a library path written with a `..` component. Smallest fix: test canonicalised paths in `is_inside_a_library` (falling back to the lexical test only when `canonicalize` fails), so both guards use the same notion of "the same place".

**3. P2 — the removal guard is broader than its rationale, so a staging root merely *nested* in a library leaks a duplicate of every placed album, and the warning denies it.**
Location: `src/runner.rs:432-448` (warning at `439`), `src/organizer.rs:766-777`.
`is_inside_a_library` (and `starts_with(library_root)`) fire for *any* containment, e.g. `staging_dir = /music/.staging`, where the album's library destination (`/music/Artist/Album`) is a different directory and the staging copy is exactly what the code then refuses to remove. Every placed album therefore keeps a full duplicate inside the library, and the operator is told "it lies inside a configured library path, so it is the album's library location, not a staging copy" — which is false in that case; the truthful statement is the parenthetical (keep staging outside library paths). Correct behaviour: trigger the guard on the album staging path *equalling* the write destination (`destination` is already in hand in `finish_library_write`; `album_dir` in `resume_library_upgrade`), not on containment, or at minimum reword the warning so it does not assert something untrue.

**4. P2 — recovery has no library-root guard, so the config the new guards were written for still destroys library albums that have no `processed_albums` row.**
Location: `src/organizer.rs:818-856`, `src/staging.rs:406-441`.
With `storage.staging_dir` equal to (or a parent of) a `library.paths` entry, `scan` treats the library's artist folders as artist levels and the library's album folders as staged albums; any album without a row — the normal state of a pre-existing library, since only downloads write rows — falls into the cleanup arm and is `remove_dir_all`-ed. The old code deleted even more (the whole top-level tree), so this is not a regression, but the spec's claim "A staging root inside a library root no longer truncates or deletes" is not true for the recovery path, and the only warning is the README's `staging_dir` row. Correct behaviour: either narrow that claim in the spec/README or apply the same library-root test to recovery's deletion.

**5. P2 — the forward write and recovery disagree for an album whose own title is a disc designator.**
Location: `src/organizer.rs:542-556` (`disc_subdir`) vs `src/organizer.rs:723-760` (`walk`).
For an album whose sanitised title equals the peer's marker folder (`CD 01`, `Gold (Disc 1)`), a flat file's parent equals the album root, so `disc_subdir` returns `None` and the forward copy flattens the file into the album folder (the behaviour the README now documents). `resume_library_upgrade` does not use `disc_subdir` at all: it maps every subdirectory 1:1 with a sanitised leaf, so the same file recovered after a crash lands at `<album>/Gold (Disc 1)/01 - Four.flac` — one level deeper than a completed write. Correct behaviour: state which layout wins, or make `walk` apply the same album-root test so both paths produce identical paths (the spec's rebuttal (a) covers only the forward path).

**6. P2 — README overstates what the migration does.**
Location: `README.md:264`.
"Directories written by an earlier version as a single `<artist>--<album>` folder are renamed into that shape on the next run" is not true for a legacy *multi-disc* album directory: its children are all disc folders and it holds no top-level file, so `looks_like_a_legacy_album` is false, it lands in `report.ambiguous` and is left in place (`src/staging.rs:180-189`), and recovery then skips it because of the separator (`src/staging.rs:417`). The spec records this as a deliberate limit ("a genuine legacy multi-disc album directory is not migrated automatically; the operator is told instead"), so the operator-facing text should say the same and ideally name the manual remedy.

**7. P2 — two comments claim behaviour the code does not have.**
(a) `src/runner.rs:395-397`: "The write paths guard against copying or removing in that state; this is the test they share" — `resume_library_upgrade` uses its own test (`src/organizer.rs:768`, first configured root only) rather than `is_inside_a_library`, and neither matches the "makes an album's staging path and its library destination the same directory" rationale for a merely nested staging root (finding 3).
(b) `src/staging.rs:12-19`: "Neither difference can reach a destination, because a destination component is only ever taken from a staged file's immediate parent and only when that parent is a disc designator that is not the album root itself" — for the `album: None` case the album root is *not* recognised by name (`unknown` on disk vs `Unknown` at the writer, `src/organizer.rs:771`, `967`); safety there rests solely on `unknown` not being a disc designator, which the code's own test comment (`src/organizer.rs:979-988`) states correctly. The claim is true today but the mechanism is misstated, so a future change to the placeholder would invalidate it silently.

### What I could not check

No shell access: I could not compile or run the suite, so I cannot confirm the tree builds or that the 97.13 % coverage claim in the plan note still holds. Supervisor should run `cargo test --all-targets` (and `cargo clippy --all-targets` if configured) before merge; findings 1-5 are pure code-reading results and do not depend on the commands.

### Merge verdict

**OK with notes.** Findings 2-7 are documentation/robustness issues in discouraged configurations; finding 1 is real data loss but needs three independent conditions at once (a sanitised artist name containing `--`, every staged album directory under it disc-shaped, and one stray top-level file), and the lost content is re-downloadable staging rather than library data. It should be fixed before release or explicitly recorded as an accepted limit with its trigger, which the current spec note does not do.

edits.newText:
> - **A concurrent run can still be beaten to a rename.** `merge_without_overwrite`
>   checks `target.exists()` and then renames, and `rename(2)` replaces an existing
>   file, so a second process that creates the target inside that window loses it.
>   The PID lock is what prevents two instances reaching `prepare` at once; this is
>   recorded as an assumption, not guarded further.
> - **Migration evidence must be audio.** An earlier revision treated any top-level
>   file as evidence of a legacy album directory, so a stray sidecar (`.DS_Store`,
>   `cover.jpg`, a `.part`) on an artist level whose albums were all named like disc
>   folders was enough to rename that artist's whole tree into a fabricated album
>   directory, which recovery then deleted. `looks_like_a_legacy_album` now requires
>   a top-level file that parses as audio (or a directory holding nothing at all).
>   A mixed legacy tree (top-level audio plus a disc folder) still migrates, so the
>   recursion requirement stands.
> - **Recovery deletes only download residue.** The layout makes every child of an
>   artist level look like an album, so a directory the operator put there has no
>   row and was deleted as untracked debris. The cleanup arm now removes a
>   directory only when it holds audio or a partial file; anything else is left
>   with a warning. The stale-`.part` interleaving hazard that made cleanup
>   necessary is still covered, because partial files are residue.
> - **The same-path guards test real equality, canonically.**
>   `is_the_same_dir`/`is_the_same_file` compare canonical paths, so a symlinked or
>   `.`-containing spelling of the same directory still matches; and the guard fires
>   on the album staging path *equalling* the write destination, not on containment,
>   so a staging root merely nested inside a library root still has its copy removed
>   instead of leaving a duplicate of every placed album.
> - **Recovery skips anything inside a library root.** When the staging root sits
>   inside a library path, the scan sees the library's own artist and album folders;
>   recovery now skips an entry that lies inside the library root rather than
>   deleting library albums that have no `processed_albums` row.
> - **The crash-recovery walk applies the album-root rule.** A subdirectory whose
>   sanitised name equals the album component (an album whose own title is a disc
>   designator) is flattened into the album folder, so a recovered album lands where
>   the forward write would have put it.
> - **A symlink at a merge destination is a collision, not a directory.** Renaming
>   would replace the link and recursing would follow it into an unrelated tree, so
>   the entry is skipped and reported like any other collision.
> - **Rebuttal: `..` and absolute names cannot reach the migration.**
>   `sanitize_component("..")` trims the trailing dots to nothing and returns the
>   `_` placeholder, so no directory the layout creates is named `..` or absolute;
>   a top-level entry is a real directory name, not a path expression.

<skill name="qa-gate">
# QA Gate

**Core principle:** No code ships without passing every check. Zero tolerance for skipped gates.

**Violating the letter of these gates is violating the spirit of these gates.**

## Prerequisite: Harness and Project Context

Before beginning, ensure both prerequisites are loaded:

1. If `Harness status: loaded.` is not already present as an emitted status line, load and run `harness`, then return here.
2. If `Project context status: loaded.` is not already present as an emitted status line, load and run `get-context`, then return here.

When invoked from a chain, preserve these status markers and do not repeat either prerequisite.

## Upstream Workflow Barrier

Before running any gate or classifying changed languages, check for an upstream
review workflow. Use the read-only subagent fleet/status check; this does not
dispatch subagents and is allowed even though QA gates run checks directly.

- If an active reviewer workflow is present, call `bg_wait` for its exact run
  (or all of its children) and stop this skill. Do not run QA commands on a
  tree that may still change.
- If the latest emitted `REVIEW_GATE_STATUS` is `RUNNING`, stop and let the
  originating review loop emit its terminal status.
- `CLEAN` permits QA; `BLOCKED` blocks QA: report the marker, run no gates, and
  stop until the review step re-emits `CLEAN`. An empty diff does not prove that
  an asynchronous review has finished.
- If no review step or review marker exists for standalone QA, continue.

## Gate Status Marker

Emit exactly one standalone status line when the gate finishes:

- `QA_GATE_STATUS: CLEAN` — every applicable gate ran and passed.
- `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED` — any gate failed, or a required gate could not run.

`finalising` requires the latest marker to be `CLEAN` before it presents
integration options, so a failure without this marker is invisible to the chain.
Never emit `CLEAN` when an applicable gate was skipped, could not run, or
reported findings. A gate recorded NOT APPLICABLE under the Missing-Tool Policy
was not skipped — state the reason in the report.

## When to Use

**Mandatory after all code changes and before committing or creating a PR.**

Use when:

- Implementation is complete and about to commit
- About to merge to main
- About to create a PR
- Any code change is finalised

Do NOT use for:

- Mid-implementation checkpoints (use `verify` step for those)
- Design/planning phases (no code to check)
- Review-only workflows (no code changed)

## Step 0: Detect Changed Languages

Before running any gate, identify which languages were modified:

```bash
git diff --name-only HEAD
```

Classify files by language. Run ALL applicable gates for EVERY detected language.

## Language Gates

Run in order within each detected language. Report results after each gate.
Then run the Coverage Gate and Security Gate for every detected language, and
the pre-commit fallback last.

**In a chain, do NOT fix product code.** The chain scope for `qa-gate` is gates
only: report each failure, emit `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED`, and stop. Fixes are
re-entered through the step that owns them (code-review for lint/type errors,
the implementation step for logic). Standalone runs may fix and re-run.

Gate *configuration* problems (missing tool, unparsable config) are yours to
resolve in either mode — see Auto-Generated Configs below.

**Detect existing frameworks before enforcing new ones.** For each language, first check what the project already uses — config files, test directories, `package.json` scripts, build tool plugins. Use the detected framework. Only fall back to the recommended tool from the gate table below when no existing test framework is found. Do NOT force a new test runner onto a project that already has one configured.

**Auto-generate missing tool configs.** Before running each gate, check if the tool's config file exists. If not, generate an opinionated default from the templates below. Never overwrite an existing config. Announce each generated config: `"⚙️ Generated default <tool> config: <filename>"`

| Tool | Config file to check | Default source |
| ------ | --------------------- | --------------- |
| ESLint (JS/TS) | `.eslintrc.*` or `eslint.config.*` | ESLint Default (below) |
| Prettier (JS/TS) | `.prettierrc*` or `prettier.config.*` | Prettier Default (below) |
| Biome (JS/TS) | `biome.json` | Biome Default (below) |
| ruff (Python) | `[tool.ruff]` in `pyproject.toml` | ruff Default (below) |
| mypy (Python) | `[tool.mypy]` in `pyproject.toml` | mypy Default (below) |
| pre-commit (all) | `.pre-commit-config.yaml` | pre-commit Default (below) |

When appending to `pyproject.toml`, add the section only if the table header is not already present. Do NOT duplicate existing sections.

#### ESLint Default

```json
{
  "env": { "browser": true, "es2021": true, "node": true },
  "extends": ["eslint:recommended"],
  "parserOptions": { "ecmaVersion": "latest", "sourceType": "module" },
  "rules": {
    "no-unused-vars": ["warn", { "argsIgnorePattern": "^_" }],
    "no-console": "warn",
    "eqeqeq": ["error", "always"],
    "curly": "error"
  }
}
```

#### Prettier Default

```json
{
  "semi": true,
  "trailingComma": "all",
  "singleQuote": true,
  "printWidth": 120,
  "tabWidth": 2
}
```

#### Biome Default

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://biomejs.dev/schemas/1.9.4/schema.json",
  "organizeImports": { "enabled": true },
  "linter": { "enabled": true, "rules": { "recommended": true } },
  "formatter": { "enabled": true, "indentStyle": "space", "indentWidth": 2, "lineWidth": 120 },
  "javascript": { "formatter": { "quoteStyle": "single", "semicolons": "always" } }
}
```

#### ruff Default

```toml
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
```

#### mypy Default

```toml
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_unused_configs = true
strict_optional = true
```

#### pre-commit Default

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v4.6.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-added-large-files
```

### Bash / Shell

Files matching: `*.sh`, `*.bash`, shebang `#!/bin/bash`, `#!/usr/bin/env bash`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `shellcheck $(git diff --name-only HEAD -- '*.sh' '*.bash')` |
| Format | `shfmt -d .` (diff mode — check only, do not modify) |
| Tests | Detect: if `.bats` files exist anywhere → `bats -r .`; else skip and note "No bats test files found" |

If `.bats` files exist but `bats` is not installed, skip and note it. `shellcheck` is mandatory — install it if missing.

### Python

Files matching: `*.py`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint + Format | `ruff check --fix . && ruff format .` |
| Type check | `mypy .` |
| Tests | Detect framework: if `pytest` is configured (`pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest]`, `pytest.ini`, `conftest.py`) → `pytest -v`; if `tox.ini` exists → `tox`; else `python -m unittest discover` |

Pytest is the default when no framework is detected. If a different framework is already configured, respect it.

### JavaScript / TypeScript

Files matching: `*.js`, `*.ts`, `*.jsx`, `*.tsx`, `*.mjs`, `*.cjs`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `npx eslint .` (preferred); or `npx biome check .` (if `biome.json` preferred). Config is auto-generated if missing. |
| Format | `npx prettier --check .` (preferred); Biome users: format is included in `biome check`. Config is auto-generated if missing. |
| Tests | Detect framework: check `package.json` `scripts.test` first; then look for config files — `vitest.config.*` → `npx vitest run`, `jest.config.*` → `npx jest`, `.mocharc.*` → `npx mocha`. If none found, try `npx vitest run` as default. |

Configs for ESLint, Prettier, and Biome are auto-generated if missing (see Auto-Generated Configs above). Vitest is the preferred test runner for new projects (10x faster than Jest, native ESM). If no test framework is configured, report: "No JS/TS test framework detected — add tests before merging."

### Go

Files matching: `*.go`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `golangci-lint run ./...` |
| Format | `gofmt -d .` (diff mode — check only) |
| Tests | `go test ./...` |

If `golangci-lint` is not installed, fall back to `go vet ./...`. `golangci-lint` bundles 100+ linters (vet, staticcheck, errcheck, etc.) and is the industry standard for Go.

### Rust

Files matching: `*.rs`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` |
| Format | `cargo fmt --check` |
| Tests | `cargo test` |

### Coverage Gate (all detected languages)

Measure coverage fresh on the full suite with the project's detected tool; never
reuse a number from an earlier step, because code changed since then. Use the
project's configured args and tooling; these defaults apply only when no
coverage tooling exists:

| Ecosystem | Default command |
| ----------- | ----------------- |
| Python | `pytest --cov` |
| JS/TS | `npx vitest run --coverage` (Vitest) or `npx jest --coverage` (Jest) |
| Go | `go test -cover ./...` |
| Rust | `cargo llvm-cov` |
| Other | the project's standard coverage tool, with its configured threshold |

**Threshold:** the project's configured threshold (coverage config,
`--cov-fail-under`, `coverageThreshold`, and equivalents); otherwise **95%**, the
same default as the `tech-debt` skill. Enforce with the tool's own threshold
option where available (`pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=<N>`,
`coverage report --fail-under=<N>`, Vitest/Jest `coverageThreshold`). A
`--coverage <N>` override passed in `$@` replaces the default.

If the detected test command already enforces the threshold, that run satisfies
this gate; do not measure coverage twice.

**This gate fails when** reported coverage is below the threshold, or the project
configures coverage tooling that cannot run (see Missing-Tool Policy).

### Security Gate (all detected languages)

Two fast scans. The deep OWASP/IaC/cloud review stays in the `security-audit`
skill.

**1. Dependency audit.** Use the project's installed scanner; these defaults are
the tools `security-audit` uses:

| Ecosystem | Preferred | Ephemeral fallback |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| Python | `pip-audit`, `safety`, `trivy` | `uvx pip-audit` |
| JS/TS | `npm audit` (or the detected package manager's audit) | none needed |
| Go | `govulncheck ./...` | `go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest ./...` |
| Rust | `cargo audit` | none (requires install) |
| Other | project's configured scanner | per ecosystem |

**This gate fails when** the audit reports a CRITICAL or HIGH advisory, or an
advisory the tool does not classify. MEDIUM and LOW advisories are informational
records, not gate findings: list them in the report.

**2. Secret scan of changed files.** Run the project's configured scanner if it
has one (`gitleaks detect --source . --no-git`, `trufflehog filesystem .`, or
`detect-secrets scan`). With no scanner configured, review the changed files and
diff against the secrets checklist in the `security-audit` skill's secrets phase
(credential-named variables, config files, connection strings, base64 blobs,
CI/IaC files).

**This gate fails on any confirmed secret** in the changed files. Verify
placeholders and sanitized examples before reporting, and record what was
checked.

### Missing-Tool Policy (Coverage and Security Gates)

Run the tool ephemerally where the ecosystem supports it (`uvx pip-audit`,
`go run ...govulncheck`). Never install a dependency to run a gate: record
`not run - tool absent` and mark that gate **NOT APPLICABLE**.

Exception: a tool the project already configures (config file, script, CI job,
pre-commit hook) is required: failing to run it is a **FAILED** gate.

Never emit `FAILED` only because the project has never used a coverage or
security tool; never emit `CLEAN` over a configured tool you did not run.

### Fallback: Pre-commit (All Languages)

Always run last, regardless of detected languages. If `.pre-commit-config.yaml` does not exist, auto-generate the default config (see Auto-Generated Configs above) before running.

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

**Do NOT commit** — this is verification only. In a chain, report failures and
stop; do NOT fix product code. Standalone runs may fix and re-run until clean.

### Auto-Detection (Languages Without Explicit Gates)

For files in languages not listed above, detect the project type from config files and run appropriate checks. Do NOT skip to a manual review — this is an automated gate.

**Detection table — scan for these project files and run the corresponding commands:**

| Config file | Language | Test command | Lint/check command |
| ------------- | ---------- | ------------- | ------------------- |
| `package.json` | JS/TS | `npm test` | `npx eslint .` (if configured) |
| `go.mod` | Go | `go test ./...` | `golangci-lint run ./...` (fall back to `go vet ./...`) |
| `Cargo.toml` | Rust | `cargo test` | `cargo clippy` |
| `Gemfile` | Ruby | Detect: `bundle exec rspec` (if `spec/` or `.rspec` exists), else `bundle exec rake test` (minitest) | `bundle exec rubocop` |
| `pom.xml` | Java | `mvn test` | `mvn checkstyle:check` (if plugin configured) |
| `build.gradle*` | Java/Kotlin | `gradle test` | `gradle check` (if checkstyle/spotless configured) |
| `CMakeLists.txt` | C/C++ | `ctest` | `cppcheck .` (or `clang-tidy` if `compile_commands.json` exists) |
| `Makefile` | C/C++ | `make test` (if target exists) | `cppcheck .` (or `clang-tidy` if `compile_commands.json` exists) |

**Procedure:**

1. Run `find . -maxdepth 2 \( -name 'package.json' -o -name 'go.mod' -o -name 'Cargo.toml' -o -name 'Gemfile' -o -name 'pom.xml' -o -name 'build.gradle*' -o -name 'CMakeLists.txt' \) 2>/dev/null` to find project configs.
2. For each match, run the corresponding test and lint commands from the table.
3. If a tool is not installed, skip it and note the skip — but tests must still pass via whatever runner IS available.
4. If NO config file is detected at all, ask the user: "No test framework detected for changed files. Which test/lint commands should I run?" and wait for input. Do NOT skip to a manual review without user input.

## The Iron Law

```
ALL GATES FOR ALL DETECTED LANGUAGES MUST PASS BEFORE PROCEEDING
```

No skipping. No "it's just a warning." No "I already ran that." Run every gate, report every result.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --------- | ----- |
| Skipping shellcheck because "it's just a script" | Shell scripts run in production. Lint them. |
| Skipping bats because "I tested manually" | Manual testing is not repeatable. Run bats. |
| Skipping ruff because "formatting is cosmetic" | Ruff catches bugs too. Run it. |
| Accepting mypy `# type: ignore` without investigation | Every ignore is a potential runtime error. Fix the type. |
| Skipping a "flaky" test | Flaky tests hide real bugs. Investigate and fix. |
| Skipping lint/format because "no config exists" | Auto-generate a default config. No gate should skip for missing config — the templates are provided in this skill. |
| Treating auto-detection as optional — "it's not in the explicit gates list" | The auto-detection table IS a gate. Run it for every detected config file. |
| Running pre-commit after committing | Run it BEFORE committing. Verification gate, not cleanup. |
| Only running gates for one language in a multi-language change | Every changed language gets every gate. |
| Re-using cached results from earlier | Run fresh. Cached results hide regressions. |
| Fixing product code during an in-chain QA run | QA verifies. Report the failure, emit `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED`, and let the owning step fix it. |
| Forcing a new test framework onto an existing project | If the project already has configured tests (config files, scripts.test, test directories), use them. Only pick a default when nothing exists. |
| Reusing the coverage number from an earlier step | Code changed since then. Measure coverage fresh on the final tree. |
| Skipping a scanner the project never configured | Run it ephemerally first (`uvx pip-audit`); only then record NOT APPLICABLE. |
| Emitting FAILED because the project never had coverage/security tooling | That is NOT APPLICABLE under the Missing-Tool Policy, not a gate failure. |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
| -------- | --------- |
| "shellcheck shows style warnings — that's fine" | ShellCheck warnings catch real bugs. Fix them. |
| "the bash script is too simple to need bats" | Simple scripts break. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "ruff shows warnings but no errors — that's fine" | Warnings become errors in CI. Fix them now. |
| "mypy only has one error, I'll skip it" | One type error = one guaranteed runtime crash path. |
| "that test is flaky, not my fault" | Your code is in the repo. Flaky tests are your problem. |
| "pre-commit would pass if I committed" | The gate is verification. Run it without committing. |
| "I ran these in a previous step" | Code changed since then. Run them again fresh. |
| "the CI will catch this" | CI is not your personal QA gate. Run it locally. |
| "only Python files changed, I'll skip the bash gates" | You changed bash files. Run the bash gates. |
| "no ESLint config exists, so I'll skip lint" | Auto-generate `.eslintrc.json` from the template. A missing config is not a valid reason to skip. |
| "no Prettier config exists, skipping format" | Auto-generate `.prettierrc` from the template. Format should never be skipped for missing config. |
| "no pre-commit config exists, skipping" | Auto-generate `.pre-commit-config.yaml` from the template. Every project needs pre-commit validation. |
| "I'll just fix this one type error myself" | In a chain that is the code-review step's job. QA mutation hides the failure from the gate marker. |
| "Coverage is tech-debt's problem" | tech-debt fixes coverage earlier in the chain; QA verifies the final tree still meets the threshold. |
| "The dependency audit isn't one of this skill's gates" | It is now: CRITICAL/HIGH advisories fail the Security Gate. |
| "I'll route the advisory to a later step instead of failing" | Findings that meet a gate's fail conditions ARE the gate failure. Emit FAILED. |
| "The CVE can be fixed after release" | Known HIGH/CRITICAL advisories block QA. That is the point of the gate. |

## Red Flags — STOP

- "shellcheck shows style warnings — that's fine"
- "the bash script is too simple to need bats"
- "ruff shows warnings but no errors — that's fine"
- "mypy only has one error, I'll skip it"
- "cargo clippy warnings are just style — they're fine"
- "go vet warnings are informational — I'll skip them"
- "the test is flaky, not my fault"
- "pre-commit would pass if I committed"
- "I ran these in a previous step"
- "the CI will catch this"
- "only Python changed, I'll skip bash gates"
- "no config exists for X — I'll skip that gate" (auto-generate it instead)
- "this language isn't in the explicit gates list — I'll just do a manual review" (use auto-detection instead)
- "the project uses Jest but Vitest is faster — I'll switch it" (respect existing framework configuration)
- "I'll fix it myself before reporting" (in a chain, report and stop)
- "coverage was already checked earlier in the chain"
- "the dependency audit isn't one of this skill's gates"
- "I'll route the advisory forward instead of failing"
- "no scanner is installed, so there is nothing to check"
- "we'll fix the CVE after release"

**All of these mean: run the gate you're trying to skip. Every language, every gate, every time.**
</skill>
